title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting
summary: Financial time series exhibit multi-scale, high-noise, and non-stationary volatility dynamics. Decomposition--integration frameworks built on complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) have advanced this field, yet existing CEEMDAN hybrids remain unstable: high-frequency mode mixing contaminates downstream predictors, and the heterogeneous volatility of decomposed components is not matched by any volatility-adaptive mechanism. To address these gaps, this paper proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL. CEEMDAN adaptively decomposes the original series, and sample-entropy-driven K-means clustering groups the intrinsic mode functions into high-, mid-, and low-frequency and residual components. Singular spectrum analysis (SSA) is then applied to the high-frequency group, whose singular-value decomposition of the trajectory matrix and principal-component reconstruction decouple intertwined pseudo-oscillatory modes and alleviate mode mixing. We further design a plug-and-play robust LSTM variant, the volatility-modulated GARCH-LSTM (VMGL), which embeds a differentiable GARCH(1,1) layer inside the LSTM cell as a risk gate; the estimated conditional volatility multiplicatively scales the forget-gate activation, letting memory decay adapt to the instantaneous volatility while remaining fully end-to-end trainable. Component predictions are linearly combined. On five US and Chinese financial series (CSI 300, CSI 500, AAPL, GOOGL, S&P 500), the proposed model is compared with eleven benchmark architectures, lowering the forecasting error by 9% to 24% relative to the best benchmark and by 60% to 70% relative to a standard LSTM. Diebold--Mariano and model-confidence-set (MCS) tests confirm the statistical significance and stability of the gains, spectral analyses verify the SSA denoising efficacy, and backtesting demonstrates the framework's economic utility.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a novel decomposition-integration framework combining CEEMDAN (Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise) with singular spectrum analysis (SSA) for denoising high-frequency modes and introduces a volatility-modulated GARCH-LSTM (VMGL) for adaptive forecasting. The framework includes sample-entropy-driven K-means clustering for component grouping and volatility-aware LSTM cells.
data_sources: The model is tested on five financial series: CSI 300, CSI 500 (Chinese indices), AAPL, GOOGL (US stocks), and S&P 500 (US index).
alpha_potential: The framework addresses key challenges in financial time series forecasting, such as high noise and non-stationary volatility, by combining decomposition techniques with a volatility-adaptive LSTM. The reported error reductions (9-24% vs benchmarks, 60-70% vs standard LSTM) and backtested economic utility suggest strong potential for extracting alpha from volatility and multi-scale price dynamics.
title_cn: 基于奇异谱分析和波动率自适应LSTM的股票价格预测分解-集成框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL框架，通过自适应分解、熵聚类和奇异谱分析降噪，并设计波动率调制GARCH-LSTM单元，实现对多尺度金融时序的精准预测。在中美五大金融标的上显著超越基准模型，误差降低9%-24%，具有明确的量化交易应用价值。

title: Learning volatility-adaptive forgetting via GARCH-modulated LSTM for stock price forecasting
summary: Stock price forecasting is hindered by the heteroscedastic nature of financial time series, in which turbulent and tranquil regimes alternate. Although the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is widely used for this task, its gates are oblivious to such volatility variation, so memory retention remains fixed regardless of market conditions. A common remedy is to supply volatility estimates as an additional input feature, yet this leaves the internal memory dynamics untouched. Instead, volatility can serve as a direct regulatory signal over the gate activation itself. This paper presents the Gsigmoid-LSTM model, which embeds Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (GARCH(1,1))-derived volatility estimates into the LSTM forgetting gate through the Gsigmoid activation function, a volatility-adaptive variant of the sigmoid that combines a volatility adjustment factor with slope regulation via a learnable parameter. The model thereby automatically prioritizes recent information during turbulent periods while preserving long-term dependencies in stable markets. In the engineering application of daily stock price forecasting, extensive experiments, including activation function comparisons, baseline evaluations, and ablation studies, demonstrate that this structural gating modification effectively improves forecasting accuracy and robustness. The proposed model significantly outperforms a feature-level fusion baseline carrying the same volatility signal on all five datasets, as confirmed by Diebold-Mariano tests with all p<0.01, attains the best average rank of 1.00 in the Friedman test across nine models, and achieves the lowest MSE and MAE on all five datasets.
core_methodology: The paper proposes the Gsigmoid-LSTM model, which integrates GARCH(1,1)-derived volatility estimates into the LSTM forgetting gate through a volatility-adaptive activation function (Gsigmoid). This allows the model to dynamically adjust memory retention based on market volatility, prioritizing recent information during turbulent periods and preserving long-term dependencies in stable markets.
data_sources: The model is tested on daily stock price data from five datasets, though the specific stocks or markets are not mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to adapt to varying volatility regimes can capture market inefficiencies related to volatility clustering and regime shifts, potentially improving forecasting accuracy and robustness in trading strategies.
title_cn: 通过GARCH调制的LSTM学习波动率自适应遗忘机制用于股票价格预测
summary_cn: 该研究提出Gsigmoid-LSTM模型，通过将GARCH(1,1)波动率估计嵌入LSTM遗忘门，实现根据市场波动自动调节记忆保留。此结构改进显著提升预测精度，在五个数据集上均实现最低MSE和MAE，验证了其在动荡市场优先新信息、稳定市场保持长期依赖的能力，对量化交易中基于波动率调整的策略具有直接应用价值。

title: Paloma: Phase-Conditioned Residual Modulation for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Explicitly modeling periodicity has proven to be an efficient approach for time series forecasting, where the residual, obtained after removing the periodic component from the time series, is typically treated as unstructured noise. However, in this work, we show that such residuals still exhibit structured, \textit{phase-dependent} deviations, as supported by both empirical observations and theoretical analysis. This suggests that residuals should not be treated merely as unstructured noise, but instead as \textit{phase-conditioned signals} whose variations arise in both direction and magnitude. Motivated by this perspective and inspired by phase and amplitude modulation in classical signal processing, we propose \textit{Paloma}, a simple yet effective framework for modeling residual deviations. Specifically, Paloma comprises two complementary modules: \textit{a Phase Rotation module}, which performs phase-conditioned rotations to capture directional changes in the feature space, and \textit{an Amplitude Scaling module}, which applies phase-conditioned affine transformations to model magnitude variations. We further abstract the two modules into a general-purpose plugin, termed the \textit{Paloma technique}, which can be readily integrated into existing forecasting architectures to modulate input sequences in a phase-aware manner, enabling backbone models to capture phase-dependent variations in both direction and magnitude. Extensive experiments on twelve datasets demonstrate that Paloma achieves state-of-the-art and robust forecasting performance. Additional results show that the Paloma technique consistently improves a wide range of baseline models, validating its effectiveness as a general-purpose component. Our Code is available at \url{https://github.com/TSTS13/Paloma}.
core_methodology: Paloma is a framework that models residual deviations in time series data through phase-conditioned rotations (Phase Rotation module) and affine transformations (Amplitude Scaling module), inspired by phase and amplitude modulation in signal processing. It abstract these into a general-purpose plugin (Paloma technique) that can be integrated into existing forecasting models to capture phase-dependent variations in direction and magnitude.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but the methodology is applicable to any periodic time series data, making it suitable for financial market data like stock prices, FX rates, or economic indicators.
alpha_potential: Paloma's ability to capture phase-dependent residual patterns could identify new market inefficiencies or improve existing forecasting models, particularly in strategies relying on periodic or seasonal patterns (e.g., intraday strategies, earnings season effects, or macroeconomic cycles).
title_cn: Paloma：基于相位条件残差调制的时间序列预测方法
summary_cn: Paloma通过相位旋转和幅度缩放模块建模时间序列中的残差偏差，能捕捉相位相关的方向和幅度变化。该方法可作为通用插件整合至现有预测模型中，适用于金融市场数据，提升周期性交易策略的信号质量，如日内交易或宏观经济周期策略。

title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models
summary: Modeling limit order book (LOB) dynamics is central to market forecasting and execution-strategy evaluation. While diffusion models achieve strong empirical performance, existing LOB snapshot models typically lack a learned recurrent encoder and formal statistical guarantees. We introduce LOBGrad, a conditional DDPM framework for probabilistic LOB forecasting that combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion-based generator. In particular, we establish an excess-risk oracle inequality for the one-step DDPM noise-prediction objective under exponential mixing and regularity assumptions. We further show that, under contractive dynamics, the dependence on the conditioning-window length can be reduced to a dependence on the latent-state dimension. Experiments on BTC/USDT, GOOGL, and META show that LOBGrad improves on its encoder-free diffusion ablation across all reported queue metrics and obtains competitive results against other baselines. It also reproduces the key stylized facts of LOB microstructure, and yields reasonably calibrated queue-based predictive intervals. A stylized downstream task illustrates the potential value of the generated forecasts.
core_methodology: Combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) for probabilistic forecasting of limit order book dynamics, with theoretical guarantees under specific conditions.
data_sources: BTC/USDT (cryptocurrency), GOOGL, and META (equities) limit order book data.
alpha_potential: High potential for improving execution strategies and short-term market predictions by capturing LOB microstructure dynamics and generating calibrated predictive intervals, particularly useful for HFT and market-making strategies.
title_cn: 基于条件扩散模型的概率化订单簿预测
summary_cn: LOBGrad框架创新性地结合了自回归RNN编码器与条件扩散模型，实现对订单簿动态的概率化预测，并在BTC/USDT、GOOGL和META数据上验证了其在队列指标预测和微观结构特征重现方面的优势。该方法生成的校准预测区间可显著优化高频交易执行策略，为做市商提供实时决策支持。

title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
summary: While autoregressive foundation models trained on limit order book (LOB) data show state-of-the-art performance for market simulation, pre-training with cross-entropy neither penalizes the compounding of sampling errors over free-running rollouts nor targets desired market properties. We introduce a post-training method for LOB foundation models using a Wasserstein generative adversarial network (GAN) objective. A critic, trained online on rollouts through the true, non-differentiable matching engine, guides updates from evolution strategies over rank-4 LoRA perturbations of the pre-trained generator, under a KL trust region. For efficiency, we use EGGROLL (Evolution Guided GeneRal Optimisation via Low-rank Learning), a memory-efficient variant of evolution strategies. On a held-out panel, adversarial post-training improves LOB-Bench realism by 17.6% (WS-21) and 17.0% (Mean-$L_1$), while selection-matched random-perturbation and compute-matched continued-pre-training controls yield no improvement. Post-training is thus a necessary stage that more pre-training does not replace. Per-position divergence measurements show that it slows error accumulation over 500-message rollouts from $3.1\times$ to $2.3\times$. Adversarial post-training is also inexpensive, requiring under 50M training tokens and 12 GPU-hours per seed, three orders of magnitude below the 48B-token pre-training budget. Ablations over critic inputs, optimizers, and the population-rollout trade-off, together with an analysis of reward hacking, yield practical design guidelines for adversarial post-training.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an adversarial post-training method for limit order book (LOB) foundation models using a Wasserstein GAN objective. A critic trained online on rollouts through the true, non-differentiable matching engine guides updates from evolution strategies over rank-4 LoRA perturbations of the pre-trained generator, under a KL trust region. The method uses EGGROLL, a memory-efficient variant of evolution strategies, to improve the realism of market simulations.
data_sources: Limit order book (LOB) data, which is crucial for high-frequency trading and market microstructure analysis.
alpha_potential: The adversarial post-training method improves the realism of market simulations by 17.6% (WS-21) and 17.0% (Mean-$L_1$), which can lead to more accurate predictions of market behavior and better trading strategies. The method also slows error accumulation over 500-message rollouts, making it more reliable for high-frequency trading applications.
title_cn: 基于对抗性后训练的基础模型在高频交易中的应用
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种用于限价订单簿（LOB）基础模型的对抗性后训练方法，利用Wasserstein GAN目标提高市场模拟的真实性。通过在线训练一个评论家模型，引导进化策略对预训练生成器进行低秩扰动更新，该方法显著提升了市场模拟的准确性（WS-21提升17.6%，Mean-$L_1$提升17.0%），降低了误差累积速度，适用于高频交易策略开发。

title: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator-Critic Trading Systems
summary: Generator--critic trading systems pair an LLM-based trader that makes trading decisions with a red team agent that evaluates these decisions and provides feedback for revision. However, improving individual trading decisions does not ensure that both agents learn from experience and improve together over time. This raises an important question: how can the trader and red-Team select useful experience and learn from each other's evolving behavior? On one hand, experience that benefits decisions under one market condition may become ineffective or harmful under another. On the other hand, trading outcomes reflect both agents' actions, making it difficult to derive appropriate experience for each role. In this work, we propose ACE-Trader, an adversarial co-evolution trading framework. Specifically, we first develop separate context-dependent memory selectors that learn to identify useful experience for the current trading decision. Both selectors receive shared feedback from net-return differences between complete memory-assisted and memory-free trading pipelines, with online updates emphasizing recent outcomes. We further design a co-evolution mechanism that links role-specific memories through shared trading records. We use these records to evaluate the Red-Team's risk assessments and the effects of the Trader's revisions against realized market outcomes, then derive experience for their respective memories. By linking this experience to the corresponding records, we enable the Trader to improve its proposals based on prior critiques and the Red-Team to adjust its review focus as the Trader's behavior changes. Experiments on U.S. stock trading show that ACE-Trader outperforms all 22 active baselines in cumulative return and achieves the highest Sharpe ratio and lowest maximum drawdown across both active methods and passive benchmarks.
core_methodology: Adversarial co-evolution framework pairing an LLM-based trader with a red team critic, using context-dependent memory selectors and shared trading records to enable mutual learning and adaptation over time.
data_sources: U.S. stock trading data (specific tickers/exchanges not mentioned in abstract)
alpha_potential: Demonstrates improvement in cumulative returns, Sharpe ratio, and drawdowns by dynamically adapting to changing market conditions through adversarial learning and memory-assisted decision making. Outperformed 22 active baselines.
title_cn: ACE-Trader: 基于对抗协同进化的生成器-评论家交易系统
summary_cn: ACE-Trader提出了一种对抗协同进化框架，通过LLM交易员与红队评审的对抗学习，结合情境记忆选择器和共享交易记录实现双向进化。该系统在美国股票交易中展现出优异的累计收益、夏普比率和回撤控制，优于22种活跃基线策略。该方法的核心价值在于通过实时对抗学习动态适应市场变化。

title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents
summary: LLM agents can turn natural-language financial research requests into executable and backtested strategies, but a successful run may still implement the wrong rule, use information unavailable at decision time, or obscure how repairs and candidate selection changed the strategy. Because these failures arise throughout development, final code and performance metrics alone are insufficient to establish either fidelity to the request or the validity of the development process. We therefore address the reliability of financial strategy development at the trajectory level: the system must control how intermediate outputs become downstream state and preserve the evidence needed to justify the terminal outcome. We introduce QuantHarness, a two-layer agent harness in which a finance-specific Workflow structures specification, data grounding, construction, testing, and review, while Harness Core enforces stage-specific information, action, and commitment boundaries. We also introduce FinRelBench, a benchmark that evaluates strategy-development reliability through execution success, requirement satisfaction, and runtime evidence. QuantHarness achieves the highest Task Success at 90.72\%, compared with 74.23\%--84.54\% for the comparison systems. Controlled stress tests show that its boundaries contain targeted violations, while structured run records improve evidence retrieval and support decision replay under the evaluated protocol.
core_methodology: Two-layer agent harness system combining finance-specific Workflow (for specification, data grounding, construction, testing, and review) with Harness Core (enforcing stage-specific information, action, and commitment boundaries) to ensure reliable financial strategy development with LLM agents
data_sources: Not explicitly stated but implies usage of standard financial market data for strategy backtesting and execution
alpha_potential: Potential to systemize and operationalize LLM-driven strategy development while avoiding common pitfalls like look-ahead bias, logic leaks, and unreliable decision chains. The 90.72% Task Success rate suggests strong reliability in translating research requests into viable strategies
title_cn: 可靠先于盈利：QuantHarness——用LLM智能体治理金融策略开发
summary_cn: QuantHarness开发了一个双层智能体框架，通过金融专用工作流确保策略开发的全程可靠性（包含数据锚定、测试审查环节），其核心层执行严格的信息边界控制。该系统在FinRelBench测试中达到90.72%的任务成功率，能有效防止策略开发中的信息泄露和逻辑偏差，为量化交易提供了可靠的LLM策略生成解决方案。

title: AllPath: Layered Verification for a Deployed, Self-Revising LLM Trading Agent under Human-Gated and Autonomous Regimes
summary: LLM trading agents are evaluated almost exclusively in backtests and autonomous benchmark harnesses. Deployment, where actions are irreversible, raises a different question: who verifies the agent's actions, and which failures can each verifier structurally catch? We report on AllPath, a personal LLM trading agent deployed against a live paper-brokerage account. The system watches positions through a deterministic rules engine, and each night it reviews its own day and proposes revisions to its own trading strategies. Verification is split across three layers. Code verifies what must not depend on judgment: deterministic gates enforce risk limits and block any strategy revision that fails an integrity check. The agent verifies itself within fixed bounds: its nightly review has an iteration cap and no tools that can act. A human verifies judgment, through approval screens that show the current state of each proposal. We also compared two verification policies for the agent's self-revisions on the live system: two and a half weeks with every self-revision human-gated, then five weeks with reflection revisions auto-applied behind the same code gates, while the operator's chat channel stayed human-gated throughout. Each layer caught a different kind of failure. The code gates rejected no proposal; their role was keeping revisions consistent. The human rejected two proposals that passed every code check, both over a disagreement about the market, and later removed 11 of the 19 rules the agent had added on its own, at a median lag of eight days. The most instructive production incidents, such as strategies silently left unmonitored, passed every gate; the operator found them by hand, and the fix each time was an interface change that makes the condition visible. We contribute the layered architecture, the two-regime account, and a production incident taxonomy, none observable in a backtest.
core_methodology: Layered verification architecture for a deployed LLM trading agent, combining deterministic code gates, self-review with iteration caps, and human oversight to ensure safe and effective trading decisions.
data_sources: Live paper-brokerage account data, including position tracking and market conditions.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha from continuous self-improvement of trading strategies through nightly reviews and revisions, with human oversight to mitigate overfitting or market misjudgments.
title_cn: AllPath：部署的自修订LLM交易代理在人工门控和自主机制下的分层验证
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种分层验证架构，用于部署的LLM交易代理，结合确定性代码门控、有限迭代的自我审查和人工监督，以确保交易决策的安全性和有效性。通过实时账户数据和自我修订策略的持续优化，具有显著的alpha潜力，同时人工干预避免了潜在的过度拟合或市场误判。

title: Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surface Reconstruction via Additive Martingales
summary: This work focuses on reconstructing a continuous implied volatility (IV) surface from a small number of option quotes, a fundamental task for option pricing and risk management. We propose Additive Martingale (AddMart), a few-shot IV surface reconstruction framework that satisfies static no-arbitrage conditions by construction. Rather than predicting IVs directly, AddMart maps sparse quotes to non-negative increment densities of an exponential additive martingale, from which valid risk-neutral marginals and IVs are recovered. By incorporating the no-arbitrage structure directly into its architecture, rather than enforcing it through regularization in the learning objective, AddMart produces IV surfaces that satisfy static no-arbitrage conditions throughout the domain. Extensive experiments on ten real-option datasets demonstrate that AddMart achieves competitive reconstruction accuracy with no material static arbitrage violations, while directly enabling the estimation of VaR, CVaR, and crash probabilities.
core_methodology: Additive Martingale (AddMart) framework for few-shot IV surface reconstruction that inherently satisfies static no-arbitrage conditions by mapping sparse option quotes to non-negative increment densities of an exponential additive martingale, from which valid risk-neutral marginals and IVs are recovered.
data_sources: Ten real-option datasets
alpha_potential: The method provides a robust and arbitrage-free way to reconstruct IV surfaces from limited data, enabling more accurate option pricing, risk management (VaR, CVaR), and estimation of crash probabilities. This could enhance trading strategies that rely on volatility arbitrage or tail risk hedging.
title_cn: 通过可加鞅实现无套利隐含波动率曲面重构
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种通过可加鞅（AddMart）从少量期权报价中重构连续隐含波动率曲面的框架。该框架通过构造满足静态无套利条件，能够准确恢复风险中性边际和隐含波动率。实验表明该方法在多个实际期权数据集上具有竞争性的重构精度，同时可直接用于计算风险价值（VaR）、条件风险价值（CVaR）和崩盘概率，适用于期权定价和风险管理。

title: Regime-Aware Interpretable Ranking for Sector Rotation
summary: Sector rotation is a common decision in benchmark-relative portfolio management, where portfolio managers rank sectors for overweight and underweight positions. We formulate this task as ranking sector actions by expected future risk-adjusted active performance, measured with forward sector-benchmark Sharpe ratios. Such rankings should preserve temporal information, express model outputs through economically familiar signal characteristics, account for changes in signal relevance across macroeconomic environments, and capture dependencies among sectors. We propose RegimeRank, an interpretable sector-ranking model that represents fundamental and technical signals through expert-defined temporal characteristics, conditions them on learned macro factors via cross-attention, and models cross-sector dependencies through self-attention. Expected-gradient attributions identify the contributions of individual signal-transformation pairs, while macroeconomic and cross-sector attention maps provide diagnostics of the learned conditioning and relational structure. We evaluate RegimeRank on weekly S&P 500 data from 2002 to 2024 under combinatorial purged cross-validation, where it outperforms representative ranking and machine-learning baselines across multiple ranking metrics. Ablation studies support the contributions of latent macro states, regime conditioning, and cross-sector modelling, while attribution and attention analyses illustrate the temporal characteristics, macro states, and sector relationships underlying its rankings.
core_methodology: The paper proposes RegimeRank, an interpretable sector-ranking model that combines fundamental and technical signals with macroeconomic conditioning and cross-sector dependencies. It uses expert-defined temporal characteristics, conditions them on learned macro factors via cross-attention, and models cross-sector dependencies through self-attention. Attribution methods and attention maps provide interpretability.
data_sources: Weekly S&P 500 data from 2002 to 2024, covering both fundamental and technical signals as well as macroeconomic factors.
alpha_potential: The model aims to capture dynamic sector performance based on macroeconomic regimes and sector relationships, potentially identifying mispricings due to regime shifts or sector misalignment. The interpretable nature allows for practical validation of signals.
title_cn: 面向行业轮动的可解释体制感知排序模型
summary_cn: 本文提出RegimeRank模型，通过结合宏观经济体制感知和跨行业依赖关系的可解释排序方法，优化行业配置决策。模型利用注意力机制处理宏观因素和行业关系，在2002-2024年标普500数据上表现出色，为量化行业轮动策略提供了新工具。

title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
summary: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the G\^arleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.
core_methodology: The paper employs Wiener-Hopf factorization and prediction theory to solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact. It derives optimal trading policies as causal linear filters, extending to various impact decay models including exponential resilience and power-law impact.
data_sources: Theoretical in nature, but applicable to any financial market data where price impact and trading costs are measurable (e.g., equities, futures, FX).
alpha_potential: Provides a rigorous framework for extracting value from predictive signals by optimally accounting for trading frictions. Particularly valuable for high-frequency trading and execution strategies where price impact is significant.
title_cn: 最优交易过滤器与预测信号的价值
summary_cn: 本研究运用预测理论中的维纳-霍普夫分解方法，解决了具有瞬时价格影响的稳态二次交易问题。论文推导出最优交易策略作为条件预测和显式因果线性滤波器的组合，特别针对指数衰减和幂律衰减的市场影响模型提出了具体解决方案。该成果为量化交易中如何有效利用预测信号、同时考虑交易摩擦提供了理论框架，特别适用于需要精细控制交易执行的高频策略。

title: Arbitrage-Aware Probabilistic Multi-Step Forecasting of Implied Volatility Surfaces: Joint Generation of Surface-Return Trajectories Using Latent Diffusion
summary: Implied volatility surfaces summarise the option market and are central to many financial applications. Probabilistic forecasting of their future evolution requires modelling two-dimensional geometry, temporal dependence, and predictive uncertainty while preserving economic admissibility. We propose a conditional latent diffusion framework for generating joint 30-step trajectories of implied volatility surfaces and underlying returns. An arbitrage-aware autoencoder learns a surface representation, while diffusion captures the evolution. Evaluated on SPX surfaces, the framework generates realistic probabilistic multi-step scenarios. Its predictive mean also outperforms persistence beyond the shortest horizons.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a conditional latent diffusion framework for generating joint 30-step trajectories of implied volatility surfaces and underlying returns. It uses an arbitrage-aware autoencoder to learn a surface representation and diffusion models to capture the evolution.
data_sources: The framework is evaluated on SPX (S&P 500 Index) implied volatility surfaces.
alpha_potential: The methodology can generate realistic probabilistic multi-step scenarios for implied volatility surfaces, which is crucial for options trading and risk management. The predictive mean outperforms persistence beyond short horizons, indicating potential for generating actionable signals for volatility trading and arbitrage strategies.
title_cn: 基于无套利概率多步预测的隐含波动率曲面生成：利用潜在扩散联合生成曲面-收益轨迹
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种条件潜在扩散框架，用于生成隐含波动率曲面和基础收益的联合30步轨迹。通过无套利自编码器学习曲面表示，并利用扩散模型捕捉动态变化。该方法在SPX曲面上评估，能生成现实的多步概率情景，其预测均值在较长时间范围内优于持续性预测，为波动率交易和套利策略提供了潜在的应用价值。

title: Same Book, Different Fills: Partial Identification of FIFO Execution from Aggregate Order Books
summary: Price-level limit order book (L2) data reveal aggregate liquidity but not the ordered queue required by price--time priority. Passive-execution backtests can therefore depend on an unobserved cancellation-allocation rule even when observed prices, quantities, and trades are held fixed. We frame recovery of market-by-order histories from aggregate snapshots as a conditional partial identification problem: multiple histories can reproduce the same aggregate path. Holding that path, reconciled market removals, latent order partitions, and additions fixed, our path-preserving compiler varies only cancellation allocation among front, quantity-weighted-random, and back rules. Within this compiler class, we establish front--back fill ordering for a virtual tagged order during one touch-price spell. We study seven months of synchronized 2025 Tokyo Stock Exchange data for two instruments with different trading activity: RIC 1301.T and RIC 7911.T. Ten-level L2 snapshots provide book states, while L1 trades permit inference of market removals and resting side through reconciliation. Each instrument contributes 1,080 matched five-minute episodes over the same 18 held-out trading days. The aggressive benchmark is invariant across FIFO realizations, but passive execution is sensitive to the cancellation rule. For 1301.T, front rather than back cancellation raises preterminal completion by 8.01 percentage points and reduces implementation shortfall by 1.010 bps. For 7911.T, the corresponding differences are 7.39 percentage points and 0.384 bps. Thus, observationally equivalent aggregate-book paths can imply economically different passive-execution outcomes. Execution policies evaluated from aggregate data should be accompanied by FIFO sensitivity analysis rather than reported as single-point estimates based on an unobservable queue assumption.
core_methodology: The paper presents a method to recover market-by-order histories from aggregate limit order book snapshots by treating it as a conditional partial identification problem. It introduces a path-preserving compiler that varies cancellation allocation rules (front, quantity-weighted-random, back) to study their impact on passive execution outcomes.
data_sources: The study uses synchronized Tokyo Stock Exchange data for two instruments (RIC 1301.T and RIC 7911.T) over seven months. It leverages ten-level L2 snapshots for book states and L1 trades to infer market removals and resting side.
alpha_potential: The paper highlights significant economic differences in passive execution outcomes due to unobserved cancellation-allocation rules, suggesting that execution policies should incorporate FIFO sensitivity analysis. This has direct implications for optimizing execution strategies and reducing implementation shortfall.
title_cn: 同一账簿，不同填充：从聚合订单簿中部分识别FIFO执行
summary_cn: 该研究通过部分识别方法，从聚合订单簿数据中恢复市场逐笔历史，探讨不同取消分配规则对被动执行结果的影响。结果表明，观察上相同的聚合路径可能隐含显著的经济差异，为执行策略优化提供了重要启示。

title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
summary: We develop a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts. We prove that prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage and identify optimal arbitrage portfolios through integer programming. Using venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria, we recover 1.9 million logical relations and compile them into constraint systems covering more than 255,000 contracts. We replay full-depth Polymarket order books to simulate an arbitrageur executing these portfolios against resting orders. Among settled portfolios, an ideal arbitrageur that takes the full displayed depth of every opportunity and reuses its capital at resolution earns a risk-free return of 3.5% a week after spreads and fees. We find that arbitrage opportunities persist longer and attract less observed participation where relation discovery and execution are more costly.
core_methodology: The paper develops a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts using integer programming for optimal arbitrage portfolio construction. It leverages venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria to recover logical relations and compile them into constraint systems.
data_sources: Full-depth Polymarket order books, venue metadata, and semantic analysis of resolution criteria from over 255,000 contracts.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies arbitrage opportunities across prediction markets by exploiting price discrepancies outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors. An ideal arbitrageur could achieve a risk-free return of 3.5% a week after accounting for spreads and fees, indicating significant alpha potential in prediction markets.
title_cn: 预测市场中的组合套利
summary_cn: 该论文开发了一个框架，通过整数编程识别和量化预测市场中逻辑相关合约的套利机会。研究发现，价格超出可接受支付向量凸包时存在套利，模拟交易显示理想套利者可获得3.5%的周无风险回报。该方法对量化交易具有直接应用价值，尤其在预测市场的套利策略中。

title: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In?
summary: Two old market sayings hold that news is already priced in by the time it is published, and that the rumor is bought while the news is sold. Both are empirical claims about event time: they place the price move associated with a piece of news before and at publication rather than after it. Whether the claims hold, for which kinds of news, and by how much are basic questions about how fast markets absorb public information. We test them on 4.57 million financial news articles covering roughly 3,000 US stocks (2023-2026). A large language model teacher, distilled into a compact classifier through active learning, assigns each article one of 17 event tags and five attributes; articles are clustered into stories to separate first reports from follow-up coverage; and beta-adjusted abnormal returns are measured around the resulting 1.68 million stock-day events, with 364{,}405 neutral-sentiment events as a placebo group. Three results follow. First, the price move associated with news concentrates before and at publication: pooled across all signed events, the cumulative move in the news direction by the close of publication day is 2.8 times its value twenty days later, and for rumor-flagged events the directional return is concentrated around the rumor event, with little incremental return at the subsequent linked non-rumor event. Second, measured against the placebo of comparable stocks, markets underreact to numbers and overreact to stories: quantified fundamental news (earnings, dividends, guidance, analyst actions) keeps drifting in the direction of the news for weeks, while soft story-driven news (launches, macro commentary, leadership) gives back its move. Third, news carries width as well as direction: neutral news raises publication-day volatility. The study also produces a table of measured drift for each event tag, usable as a prior in news-conditioned forecasting models.
core_methodology: The study uses a large language model (LLM) to classify and tag financial news articles, then applies event study methodology with beta-adjusted abnormal returns to analyze market reactions before, during, and after news publication. The approach includes clustering articles into stories to separate first reports from follow-up coverage.
data_sources: 4.57 million financial news articles covering approximately 3,000 US stocks from 2023 to 2026. The study also uses a placebo group of 364,405 neutral-sentiment events for comparison.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies distinct market behaviors: underreaction to quantified fundamental news (e.g., earnings, dividends) which leads to post-news drift, and overreaction to soft story-driven news (e.g., launches, macro commentary) which results in price reversals. These findings can be leveraged to design momentum or mean-reversion strategies based on news type. The volatility increase around neutral news also suggests potential for volatility-based strategies.
title_cn: 买入谣言，卖出新闻：信息何时被定价？
summary_cn: 本研究通过分析457万篇金融新闻，发现市场对量化基本面新闻（如盈利、股息）反应不足导致后续漂移，对软性新闻（如产品发布、宏观评论）过度反应导致价格反转。这些模式可用于设计基于新闻类型的动量或均值回归策略。中性新闻还会增加当日波动性，为波动率策略提供机会。

title: Dynamical Kernel Attention: Estimating the Present from a Record of the Past
summary: Standard self-attention compares tokens by similarity but does not account for how much of a past state survives to the present. We introduce Dynamical Kernel Attention (DKA), which derives attention from robust estimation of a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics. As a past state decays toward equilibrium under the dynamics, the information it carries about the present vanishes, bounding the total evidence a head can draw. Unlike recency biases, DKA can abstain when relevant evidence is weak and guarantees a bounded error when old tokens are discarded. DKA preserves the parallel structure and computational cost of standard attention. We present the model and its theory; empirical evaluation is deferred to a subsequent version.
core_methodology: Dynamical Kernel Attention (DKA) extends standard self-attention by incorporating latent state evolution under stochastic dynamics, providing bounded error guarantees for attention mechanisms.
data_sources: Not explicitly stated in the abstract, but likely requires sequential data (e.g., time series of market prices, order book data, or alternative datasets with temporal dependencies).
alpha_potential: The method's ability to robustly estimate relevant temporal dependencies and abstain from weak evidence suggests potential for improving momentum strategies, event-driven models, or any trading signal relying on time-decaying information.
title_cn: 动态核注意力机制：依据历史记录估算当前状态
summary_cn: 动态核注意力机制(DKA)引入基于潜在状态随机演化的鲁棒性估计,可自动屏蔽失效历史信息并确保有限误差。这一特性在量化交易中可优化动量策略的信号处理,提高对市场时变规律的捕捉能力。

title: From SEC Filings to Financial Signals: Evaluating LLMs on Stock Market Reactions and Analyst Forecasts
summary: Form 10-Q MD&A sections combine long-form management narrative with accounting and forward-looking information. Benchmarks for financial filings commonly evaluate question answering or numerical reasoning, leaving unclear whether outputs from large language models (LLMs) align with market and analyst outcomes. We evaluate prompted, zero-shot outputs from 13 general-purpose and finance-specialized LLMs on 45,964 Form 10-Q filing events from 2001 to 2024, linking MD&A text to cross-sectional fundamental ranks, pre-filing analyst forecasts, and realized abnormal returns. The evaluation covers return ranking under five controlled information views and next-quarter EPS forecasting under direct and consensus-anchored interfaces. Relative to disclosure alone, adding cross-sectional fundamental ranks raises mean effective-date rank correlation (RankIC) by 0.0089 for effective-event-date returns and 0.0098 for following-day returns, whereas analyst-summary context provides no comparable average gain. Across the four disclosure-containing views, finance-specialized models show an effective-event-date group advantage but no statistically reliable following-day advantage, while general-purpose Qwen models produce the strongest individual return-ranking results. Under the full-information view, direct LLM forecasts average the 43.4th percentile of the analyst distribution and do not consistently beat individual analysts. Consensus anchoring raises the mean inside-range share from 41.1% to 59.5% but increases reported-EPS error.
core_methodology: The paper evaluates the performance of 13 general-purpose and finance-specialized LLMs on extracting financial signals from Form 10-Q MD&A sections. It links LLM outputs to cross-sectional fundamental ranks, analyst forecasts, and realized abnormal returns, using five controlled information views for return ranking and next-quarter EPS forecasting.
data_sources: 45,964 Form 10-Q filing events from 2001 to 2024, including MD&A text, cross-sectional fundamental ranks, pre-filing analyst forecasts, and realized abnormal returns.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that LLMs can extract meaningful signals from financial disclosures, particularly when combined with cross-sectional fundamental ranks. Finance-specialized models show effective-date advantages in return ranking, suggesting potential alpha generation from timely interpretation of management narratives in regulatory filings.
title_cn: 从SEC文件到金融信号：评估LLMs在股市反应和分析师预测中的表现
summary_cn: 本研究评估了13种通用和金融专用LLMs从10-Q文件管理层讨论部分提取金融信号的能力，重点分析了模型输出与横截面基本面排名、分析师预测和异常回报的关系。研究发现金融专用模型在事件日回报排名中表现出优势，同时在结合基本面排名时信号质量提升，为利用监管文件文本开发交易策略提供了实证依据。

title: Unbounded Losses, Unchecked Inputs: Measuring the Safeguards of LLM Options-Trading Agents
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents now place options orders at retail brokers, and developers publish open-source options agents faster than anyone has examined them. Prior security work on trading agents scored academic equities designs by whether an attacker can flip a buy-or-sell decision. We present the first measurement of the options agents that brokers and developers ship, scored by the safeguards they enforce and by the worst loss their documented order paths can reach. We screened 765 GitHub repositories, broker documentation, and the research literature and found 215 eligible repositories and 8 broker-native agent interfaces. We then scored 26 systems, including every broker interface and every open-source project with at least 20 stars, on seven robustness and eleven security safeguards with cell-level evidence. The ecosystem is new: 198 of the 215 repositories were created in 2026, and 129 (60.0%) appeared in the two weeks around one options-trading hackathon. Of the 22 systems that can place orders, 10 enforce a pre-trade limit outside the model, yet none of the 26 authenticate their text sources or cross-check market data. Of the 26, 17 can execute with no mandatory human step and 13 can reach unbounded loss, including 6 of the 8 broker interfaces. Because an attacker who writes the agent's inputs can move an order's strike, expiry, volatility, and legs while its direction stays correct, options agents need loss limits enforced at the order boundary.
core_methodology: Measurement study evaluating the safeguards and potential risks of LLM-based options trading agents, focusing on robustness and security vulnerabilities in real-world implementations.
data_sources: 765 GitHub repositories, broker documentation (8 broker-native interfaces), and research literature (215 eligible repos). Evaluation based on 26 systems including all broker interfaces and top open-source projects (20+ stars).
alpha_potential: Identifies critical vulnerabilities in options trading automation that could expose firms to unbounded losses. Highlights the need for order boundary protections (strike/expiry validation) to prevent adversarial input manipulation - directly impacts risk management for quantitative options strategies.
title_cn: 无限亏损与未检输入：LLM期权交易代理的安全防护评估
summary_cn: 本研究首次系统评估了LLM期权交易代理的安全防护机制，发现经纪商接口及开源项目中普遍存在无限亏损风险（26个系统中有13个可达无限亏损）。关键发现包括：80%经纪商接口缺乏交易前限额，所有系统均未做文本源认证。对量化交易的直接启示：期权自动化策略需在订单边界强制实施损失限制（波动率/到期日验证），这对高频期权做市和套利策略的风控设计具有重要实践价值。

title: Morpheus-2.0: Multiscale Probabilistic Forecasting with Dual-Axis Attention
summary: A universal forecaster is trained once and applied everywhere, so it must serve tasks whose schemas, forecast horizons, and temporal resolutions all differ. The number of targets and covariates changes from dataset to dataset, horizons vary by orders of magnitude, and sampling rates range from seconds to years. Existing time-series foundation models address these only in part, since they isolate each series or visit the two grid relations in separate blocks, and they fix the horizon and resolution before training begins. We introduce Morpheus-2.0, a compact encoder-only foundation model that represents targets and covariates on a single variable-time grid. Its dual-axis attention runs both relations side by side in every layer, one across variables at a timestep and one across time within a variable; a learned gate weights the two per layer, and an axis-aware rotary encoding preserves both grid coordinates. The forecast length is sampled during training, so one set of weights spans short to long horizons at no additional inference cost. Morpheus-2.0 Multiscale extends the model to several temporal resolutions at once, weighting them according to the series being forecast. Across GIFT-Eval, which spans several domains and frequencies, the two models give complementary operating points: Morpheus-2.0 attains 0.685 relative MASE with 81M parameters, while the larger Morpheus-2.0 Multiscale attains 0.646 relative MASE and 0.455 relative CRPS, the lowest of any published system on both metrics.
core_methodology: Morpheus-2.0 introduces a compact encoder-only foundation model for universal time-series forecasting. It uses dual-axis attention (across variables at a timestep and across time within a variable) with learned gating and axis-aware rotary encoding. The model also implements multiscale forecasting by weighting different temporal resolutions adaptively.
data_sources: GIFT-Eval dataset spanning several domains and frequencies (from seconds to years), implying compatibility with financial time-series data at various resolutions.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to handle varied forecast horizons (from short to long) and multiple temporal resolutions simultaneously could uncover multi-scale market inefficiencies. The dual-axis attention may capture both cross-asset relationships and temporal patterns more effectively than traditional approaches.
title_cn: Morpheus-2.0：基于双轴注意力的多尺度概率预测模型
summary_cn: Morpheus-2.0提出了一种新型时间序列基础模型，通过双轴注意力和多尺度预测机制，可同时处理不同时间分辨率和预测周期的金融数据。该模型有望用于开发跨资产、多时间维度的量化交易策略，特别适用于捕捉市场中的多尺度价格模式。

title: Revisiting Smoothed Online Learning: Competitive Ratio, Dynamic Regret with Switching Cost, and Best of Both Worlds
summary: We revisit smoothed online learning and develop algorithms with improved competitive ratios, optimal dynamic regret with switching cost, and best-of-both-worlds guarantees. Surprisingly, minimizing the hitting cost alone is $\max(1,\frac{2}{\alpha})$-competitive for $\alpha$-polyhedral functions under the $\ell_2$-norm switching cost and $1+\frac{4}{\lambda}$-competitive for $\lambda$-quadratic growth functions under the squared $\ell_2$-norm switching cost, significantly improving existing guarantees. The polyhedral bound is tight for this naive algorithm, and we establish a matching lower bound for $\alpha\geq1$. For convex $\lambda$-quadratic growth hitting costs, minimizing a suitably weighted sum of hitting and squared $\ell_2$-norm switching costs yields a competitive ratio of $1+\frac{2}{\sqrt{\lambda}}$. For dynamic regret with the $\ell_2$-norm switching cost, we develop Smoothed Ader (SAder), which achieves the optimal $O(\sqrt{T(1+P_T)})$ rate in the standard online convex optimization setting, where $P_T$ is the comparator's path-length. Its lookahead version removes the bounded-gradient assumption, and a matching lower bound establishes optimality in this setting. Finally, for convex hitting costs on a bounded convex domain, we develop UDNP to aggregate any two experts in the lookahead setting under both switching costs. Its additional cumulative cost is at most $O(1)$ relative to the first expert and $O(\sqrt{T\log T})$ relative to the second, yielding best-of-both-worlds guarantees without bounded gradients.
core_methodology: Smoothed online learning algorithms with improved competitive ratios and dynamic regret bounds, focusing on polyhedral and quadratic growth functions under different switching costs.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to various data sources including financial time series (e.g., asset prices, returns, volatility) where online learning and switching costs are relevant.
alpha_potential: Potential for portfolio optimization under transaction costs (modeled as switching costs) and dynamic asset allocation strategies where minimizing both prediction error (hitting cost) and turnover (switching cost) is crucial.
title_cn: 重温平滑在线学习：竞争比率、带切换成本的动态后悔及双优保证
summary_cn: 本研究改进了平滑在线学习算法，显著提升了竞争比率和动态后悔边界，特别适用于带交易成本的量化交易策略。核心创新包括针对多面体函数和二次增长函数的最优competitive ratio保证，以及优化的动态后悔算法SAder。这些理论成果可直接应用于构建低换手率的组合优化策略，在控制交易成本的同时实现稳健收益。

title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Improving every agent in an LLM-based multi-agent system can be prohibitively costly, making it important to identify which agent should be prioritized to achieve the greatest system-level gain with limited resources. Failure attribution can inform this decision, but an agent's responsibility for failures does not directly reveal the system-level gains achievable by improving it. We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an influence-function-inspired method for identifying agents with high potential for system-level improvement. For each agent, IF-MAP measures end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations, fits a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace, and uses the estimated response norm as a priority score. This black-box procedure requires no access to model parameters or gradients and produces agent priorities that can guide subsequent improvement effort. We evaluate IF-MAP across six multi-agent workflows spanning code generation, question answering, and mathematical reasoning, using the same priorities for prompt optimization and model upgrades. Optimizing the selected agents' prompts achieves a macro-average gain of 3.81 percentage points, compared with 1.85 for uniform agent selection. Across five target models, upgrading the selected agents yields macro-average gains of 7.62-16.42 percentage points, compared with 3.81-8.62 for uniform agent selection. Despite its probing overhead, IF-MAP reduces Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-V3.2 token use by 74.2% and 35.2%, respectively, relative to optimizing every agent, and reduces target-model tokens by 63.6-64.9% relative to upgrading every agent. These results support the use of IF-MAP to identify promising agents and direct improvement effort toward greater end-to-end performance gains.
core_methodology: Influence-function-inspired method for prioritizing agents in multi-agent systems by measuring end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations and fitting a regularized local response model.
data_sources: Multi-agent workflows in code generation, question answering, and mathematical reasoning, though the method is generic and could be adapted to financial data workflows.
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing multi-agent systems in algorithmic trading by identifying which agents to improve for maximum system-level performance gains, similar to portfolio optimization where selecting the right components yields outsized returns.
title_cn: IF-MAP：基于影响函数的多智能体系统中智能体优先级排序
summary_cn: IF-MAP通过受控语义提示扰动测量端到端损失变化，识别多智能体系统中对系统性能提升最具潜力的智能体。该方法无需访问模型参数，在代码生成、问答和数学推理任务中实现显著性能提升，为量化交易中的多智能体策略优化提供新思路，可类比投资组合中的最优资产选择策略。

title: Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning
summary: Transformers have emerged as a dominant architecture in modern machine learning, with in-context learning (ICL) enabling models to adapt to new tasks by conditioning on prompts, without any parameter updates. To understand the attention mechanism in transformer blocks, a growing line of theoretical work interprets ICL through the lens of classical statistical estimators. Recent works have established a connection between the attention mechanism and kernel methods, while the kernel function is usually assumed to be fixed. In practice, the query and key matrices in the attention mechanism are trained, which allows the attention mechanism to serve as an adaptive kernel method. In this work, we demonstrate that transformers can act as adaptive anisotropic kernel learners. Specifically, we study ICL for low-rank linear and multi-index nonlinear regressions, and conduct numerical simulations to show that the learned attention scores closely resemble the oracle kernels for these function classes. We then develop a general framework to analyze the generalization error of ICL by connecting transformers to the oracle kernel estimator for each function class. Our theory gives an explicit and constructive implementation of the oracle kernel estimators for these function classes using a wide and shallow transformer architecture, illustrating how the prediction is carried out by the interaction between the query token and the context tokens. Our work complements existing studies by providing numerical and theoretical evidence of how the attention mechanism adapts to anisotropic kernels in both linear and nonlinear settings.
core_methodology: The paper explores transformers as adaptive anisotropic kernel learners for in-context learning (ICL), with a focus on low-rank linear and multi-index nonlinear regressions. The work demonstrates that transformers can adapt their kernel functions dynamically, which is key for understanding how attention mechanisms can be tailored to different tasks without parameter updates.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but the methodology is generally applicable to time-series data, which is prevalent in quantitative finance (e.g., stock prices, trading volumes, macroeconomic indicators).
alpha_potential: The adaptive kernel learning capability of transformers could be leveraged to develop dynamic trading strategies that adjust to market regimes or asset-specific behaviors without retraining. This is particularly valuable for momentum strategies, factor investing, and other approaches requiring context-aware modeling.
title_cn: 跨任务自适应的核学习器：Transformers在上下文学习中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究证明Transformers可作为自适应核学习器，其动态调整的注意力机制可用于创建无需参数更新的上下文感知交易模型。这对动量策略和多因子投资具有直接应用潜力。

title: Near-Optimal Regret for Semi-Bandit Learning of Monotone Stochastic Problems
summary: We consider the task of learning an (approximately) optimal policy for stochastic optimization problems where the true distributions are unknown. In each period, the algorithm plays a policy for the stochastic problem and observes semi-bandit feedback, i.e., it only receives new samples from the random variables that were selected by the policy. We obtain an algorithm that works for a large class of ``monotone'' stochastic problems, including prophet inequality, Pandora's box, series testing, stochastic knapsack and stochastic matching. We obtain $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{nkT})$ regret for ``weakly'' monotone problems and $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{nT})$ regret for ``strongly'' monotone problems, where $T$ is the number of periods, $n$ is the problem dimension (number of random variables) and $k$ is the maximum support size of any random variable. This improves over previous regret bounds by a $\sqrt{n}$ factor. In fact, our dependence on $n$ and $T$ is the best-possible due the $\Omega(\sqrt{nT})$ lower bound for multi-armed-bandits. Our main technique is the use of Hellinger distance in bounding the ``error'' between the true and learned distributions, and the use of a constant-factor chain rule for the Hellinger distance of dependent random variables.
core_methodology: The paper presents a semi-bandit learning algorithm for stochastic optimization problems, focusing on achieving near-optimal regret bounds. The key technique involves using Hellinger distance to measure the error between true and learned distributions and applying a constant-factor chain rule for dependent random variables.
data_sources: The methodology is generic and can be applied to any stochastic optimization problem where the algorithm receives semi-bandit feedback, such as financial time series or portfolio optimization scenarios.
alpha_potential: The algorithm's ability to learn optimal policies with minimal regret in stochastic environments suggests potential applications in dynamic portfolio optimization, algorithmic trading strategies, and risk management where the underlying distributions are unknown or changing.
title_cn: 半强盗学习中单调随机问题的近优遗憾
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种用于随机优化问题的半强盗学习算法，能够以近优遗憾边界学习最优策略。通过使用Hellinger距离衡量真实与学习分布之间的误差，并结合依赖随机变量的常数因子链规则，该方法在动态投资组合优化和算法交易等金融应用中具有潜在价值。

title: No-Regret Revenue Maximization in Sequential Market Making Under Inventory Constraints
summary: Market makers keep trading efficient by setting bid and ask prices for buyers and sellers. In sequential market making, trades happen independently based on price thresholds, requiring the market maker to maintain balanced, low-risk inventory over T rounds. This paper studies how to maximize revenue with unknown buyer and seller valuations using regret minimization. When the market maker only sees trade success or failure, an algorithm achieves regret and inventory bounds proportional to T to the power of 2/3. When full order book data is available for failed trades, regret and inventory limits improve significantly to the square root of T. We also establish a fundamental trade-off via a lower bound, by proving that tighter round-by-round inventory limits strictly force higher minimum regret.
core_methodology: The paper presents a no-regret revenue maximization algorithm for sequential market making under inventory constraints. It uses regret minimization techniques to optimize bid and ask prices dynamically over T rounds, balancing revenue goals with inventory risk management. The algorithm achieves O(T^{2/3}) or O(√T) regret bounds depending on data availability.
data_sources: Trade execution data (success/failure signals) and optionally full order book data for failed trades.
alpha_potential: Addresses the core market making challenge of balancing revenue generation with inventory risk, providing a theoretically grounded approach to dynamic pricing that could outperform static spread-based market making strategies. The inventory-aware pricing could capture spread optimization alpha while controlling position risk.
title_cn: 库存约束下序列做市的无悔收益最大化
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种在库存约束下的动态做市算法，通过无悔学习技术优化买卖报价。该算法能够在T轮交易中实现O(T^{2/3})或O(√T)的遗憾上界，在控制库存风险的同时最大化收益。这种方法为电子做市商提供了理论保障的动态定价框架，相比传统固定点差策略更具优势。在完整订单簿数据可用时，性能提升显著。

title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning with General Utilities via Neural Dual Critics
summary: Reinforcement learning with general utilities optimizes nonlinear functionals of policy-induced occupancy measures. We develop a natural actor-critic method for concave RLGU objectives admitting an exact variational dual representation, with explicit constructions for a broad class of separable occupancy utilities. Rather than estimating the occupancy measure and then forming the policy-gradient pseudo-reward, our method learns this pseudo-reward directly as a function of the state-action pair using a neural critic. The critic is trained by projected stochastic updates, while multilevel Monte Carlo combines outputs across training horizons to control its bias at logarithmic expected cost. Our analysis separates conditional actor bias from estimator second moments and accounts explicitly for dual optimization, critic approximation, and neural linearization errors. Under policy-transfer, dual-stability, and local critic-regularity conditions, the method achieves $\widetilde{O}(T^{-1/2})$ global convergence above policy, critic-class, and finite-width approximation errors using $\widetilde{O}(T)$ expected environment transitions and reference samples. For a fixed critic representation, this yields $\widetilde{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ sampling complexity above the approximation floor, covering infinite state-action spaces and occupancy utilities beyond fixed finite vectors of returns.
core_methodology: A natural actor-critic method for concave reinforcement learning with general utilities (RLGU) objectives, using neural dual critics to learn pseudo-rewards directly from state-action pairs. The method employs multilevel Monte Carlo to control bias and achieves global convergence with efficient sampling complexity.
data_sources: Theoretically applicable to any environment that can be modeled with state-action pairs (e.g., market states, portfolio positions, and trading actions). Though not explicitly stated in the abstract, it could leverage market microstructure, order books, or time-series trading data as potential inputs.
alpha_potential: The methodology allows for the optimization of nonlinear functionals of policy-induced occupancy measures, which could capture complex market inefficiencies beyond simple return maximization. Potential alpha generation through adaptive policies that respond to nuanced state-action patterns in financial markets.
title_cn: 具有一般效用的样本高效强化学习：神经双重评论家方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新型强化学习方法，通过神经双重评论家直接学习状态行动对的伪奖励，优化非线性目标。在金融交易中，该方法可建立自适应策略，捕捉复杂市场状态变化，超越简单累积回报的限制。其高效样本利用率特别适用于高频或有限市场数据场景。

title: FracTS: Hierarchical and Autoregressive Time Series Generation
summary: Time series are ubiquitous across different domains, and the growing use of synthetic data for privacy-preserving sharing, data augmentation, and stress testing makes time series generation increasingly important. Early generative approaches are predominantly autoregressive, which can suffer from low sample diversity, error accumulation, and difficulty modeling long-range dependencies. In this paper, we introduce FracTS, a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine autoregressive model for multivariate time series generation. Inspired by fractal generative modeling developed for images, FracTS adapts the paradigm from 2D to 1D sequences by learning a multi-scale representation that captures global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales while following the autoregressive nature of time series. In contrast to unstructured images, time series are structured, allowing easy automated or designated temporal feature processing optimized for the model, and global (static) feature extraction describing the instances that generate the corresponding time series in the collection. We incorporate them in the generation process to further improve the generation quality. The design naturally handles multivariate dependencies and improves long-horizon temporal coherence without requiring fixed-length inputs. Experiments on five datasets (two conditional, three unconditional) conducted against seven baselines show that FracTS consistently outperforms baselines across marginal distribution and predictive ML utility, and correlation preservation in the unconditional setting. In particular, the predictive ML utility is averagely improved by 100.0% and 75.0-81.0% for unconditional and conditional time series datasets compared to the best baseline (relative error computed on dataset-averaged raw values). Code is available at: https://github.com/BetterdataLabs/fracts.
core_methodology: FracTS employs a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine autoregressive model for multivariate time series generation. Inspired by fractal generative modeling for images, it adapts the paradigm to 1D sequences by learning multi-scale representations that capture global trajectory structure at coarse scales and local dynamics at fine scales. This approach improves long-horizon temporal coherence and sample diversity while handling multivariate dependencies.
data_sources: The paper evaluates FracTS on five datasets, including both conditional and unconditional time series data. While specific financial datasets aren't mentioned, the methodology is generalizable to financial time series such as stock prices, FX rates, or alternative data streams.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to generate high-quality synthetic time series with preserved correlations and marginal distributions offers several potential applications: 1) Stress testing trading strategies with synthetic market regimes, 2) Data augmentation for rare market events, 3) Privacy-preserving sharing of proprietary trading data, 4) Simulation of multivariate financial time series for strategy development.
title_cn: FracTS：层次化自回归时间序列生成模型
summary_cn: FracTS提出了一种基于分形建模的多尺度时间序列生成方法，通过分层自回归结构同时捕捉全局轨迹结构和局部动态。该方法在保持相关性和边际分布方面优于基线模型，可应用于金融时间序列的合成数据生成、策略压力测试和数据增强等场景。

title: CVTA: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention for Multivariate Irregular Time Series Prediction
summary: Irregularly sampled multivariate time series arise in many real-world domains such as healthcare, climate science, and large-scale monitoring systems. Characterized by asynchronous observations and heterogeneity across variables, such time series pose significant challenges for forecasting. In this work, we introduce Cross-Variable Temporal Attention (CVTA), a short-term, continuous-time forecasting framework that learns prediction functions from its compact, interpretable state summarizing recent temporal dynamics across variables. CVTA uses Variable-Conditioned Embeddings to project heterogeneous variables into variable-specific latent spaces, and applies temporal attention to capture cross-variable dependencies from this state. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CVTA can be integrated as an auxiliary module into existing state-of-the-art prediction models through a dynamic meta-decision model. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world benchmarks show that CVTA achieves strong short-term predictive accuracy, supports efficient online inference, improves existing prediction models when used as an auxiliary module, and learns attention patterns that align well with domain knowledge.
core_methodology: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention (CVTA) framework for handling irregularly sampled multivariate time series by projecting variables into variable-specific latent spaces and applying temporal attention to capture cross-variable dependencies.
data_sources: Irregularly sampled multivariate time series, which can include high-frequency trading data, order book events, or other asynchronous financial market data.
alpha_potential: Potential to capture cross-asset dependencies and microstructural patterns in high-frequency trading environments, particularly useful for pairs trading, volatility forecasting, or event-driven strategies where asynchronous data is common.
title_cn: CVTA：跨变量时间注意力机制在多变量不规则时间序列预测中的应用
summary_cn: CVTA通过变量条件嵌入和时间注意力机制处理异构异步金融数据，在捕捉跨资产依赖性方面具有优势，适合高频交易中的微观结构分析和多资产联动策略开发，模型的可解释性有助于交易信号归因。

title: Distributionally-Robust Policy Learning with Observational Data
summary: Policy learning from observational data is fundamental to applications ranging from personalized medicine to welfare-program targeting, but standard approaches optimize empirical performance and may fail when the deployment distribution differs from the training distribution. We study \emph{distributionally-robust policy learning}: given observational data, we seek a policy $\pi \in \Pi$ that maximizes the worst-case policy value over an $f$-divergence ball of radius $\rho$ around the data-generating distribution. We propose an estimator built on cross-fitted doubly-robust scores for the conditional treatment effect, paired with a DRO solver that handles \texttt{KL}, $\chi^2$, and \texttt{CVaR} ambiguity sets. We establish two convergence guarantees. First, the estimated policy attains the standard $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/2})$ rate on its DRO regret, and inherits the doubly-robust property -- the rate continues to hold whenever either the outcome model or the propensity model is consistently estimated, even at slow nonparametric rates. We then propose a sample-splitting bias-correction algorithm derived from the Lagrangian dual, and show that under a Tsybakov-style margin condition on the treatment-effect, the estimator attains a fast rate of $\widetilde{O}(n^{-(1+\alpha)/(2+\alpha)})$ , interpolating between $\widetilde{O}(1/\sqrt{n})$ and $\widetilde{O}(1/n)$ as the margin parameter $\alpha$ ranges over $[0,\infty)$. To our knowledge, this is the first work to incorporate a margin condition into the analysis of distributionally-robust policy learning, and the first to obtain fast rates in this setting. Empirically, on synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments calibrated to a welfare-to-work program, distributional robustness yields meaningful improvements over empirical welfare maximization when training and test distributions differ.
core_methodology: Distributionally robust policy learning using cross-fitted doubly-robust scores for conditional treatment effects, applicable to scenarios where training and deployment distributions differ
data_sources: Observational data, potentially including financial time series, treatment effects related to trading signals, and contextual features
alpha_potential: Potential to improve trading rule robustness when market regimes change by optimizing worst-case performance across distributional shifts. Particularly relevant for factor timing strategies or regime-switching periods
title_cn: 观测数据中的分布鲁棒策略学习
summary_cn: 本研究提出的分布鲁棒策略学习方法通过优化最坏情况下的政策效果，在交易规则不同分布间保持稳健性。对量化交易的价值在于：1) 可在市场机制变化时保持策略稳定性；2) 特别适用于因子轮动和制度转换场景；3) 双稳健估计方法缓解了模型误设风险。论文获得的快速收敛率为实际交易系统实现提供了理论基础。

title: Predictive Bandit Curriculum Reinforcement Learning via Gradient-Based Sample Group Discovery
summary: Curriculum learning, which organizes training samples according to their learning priority, has been widely adopted in reinforcement learning to improve training efficiency. However, existing methods commonly construct curriculum units using predefined data properties and estimate their utility by simply aggregating a single proxy signal from recent training history.Such designs may group samples with different optimization effects and fail to anticipate how their utility evolves in relation to the policy. We propose Predictive Gradient-based Bandit (PGB) Curriculum, which first discovers optimization-aware learning units by clustering projected sample-level gradients. PGB then employs a lightweight temporal predictor to forecast the future utility of each unit and converts the predictions into a Boltzmann sampling distribution for adaptive data allocation. Experiments across multiple model scales and reasoning benchmarks show that PGB consistently outperforms standard GRPO, difficulty-based curricula, and history-based scheduling strategies, demonstrating improved data utilization and training efficiency.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Predictive Gradient-based Bandit (PGB) Curriculum, which clusters sample-level gradients to discover optimization-aware learning units and uses a temporal predictor to forecast their future utility for adaptive data allocation. This approach improves training efficiency in reinforcement learning.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources but implies a broad applicability to any data where reinforcement learning is used, potentially including financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could enhance the training of reinforcement learning models in trading strategies by optimizing the selection and scheduling of training samples, potentially leading to more robust and efficient algorithmic trading agents.
title_cn: 基于梯度样本组发现的预测性老虎机课程强化学习
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种预测性梯度老虎机课程学习方法，通过聚类样本梯度发现优化感知学习单元，预测其未来效用并自适应分配数据。此方法可提升强化学习在量化交易中的训练效率，优化交易策略的稳健性。

title: Detection Augmented Learning In Non-Stationary Bandit Environments
summary: We study the problem of non-stationary bandits without knowledge of the environmental changes. We propose Detection Augmented Learning (DAL) a black-box paradigm that comprises three modular components: a bandit algorithm, a change detector, and a forced exploration schedule. This modular design enables its applicability across a broad spectrum of bandit problems, from classical to highly structured settings. First, we provide theoretical insights into DAL's strong empirical performance: a single regret bound shows that DAL transfers the regret of its stationary input to the piecewise stationary setting, attaining or improving the best known bounds in every setting considered. We further identify conditions under which DAL performs well in drifting environments. Then, we showcase DAL's practical performance and versatility through extensive experimentation in which DAL consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods, both prior-free and prior-based, across diverse non-stationary scenarios in nine bandit settings. Finally, we investigate the effectiveness of the forced exploration and show that a bandit-driven strategy improves performance and shortens detection delay.
core_methodology: Detection Augmented Learning (DAL) combines a bandit algorithm, a change detector, and forced exploration to adapt to non-stationary environments without prior knowledge of changes. The modular design allows for broad applicability across different bandit problems.
data_sources: The paper's experiments are primarily on synthetic and simulated bandit problems, but the methodology can be applied to real-world financial data (e.g., price series, volatility measures, trading volumes) where non-stationarity is prevalent.
alpha_potential: DAL's ability to detect and adapt to regime changes in market conditions could help capture alpha by dynamically adjusting trading strategies when market behavior shifts (e.g., volatility regimes, trend reversals). The forced exploration component ensures continuous learning for new regimes.
title_cn: 非稳态多臂老虎机环境中的检测增强学习
summary_cn: 本文提出的检测增强学习（DAL）框架通过结合赌博算法、变化检测器和强制探索机制，能够在市场环境突变时自动调整策略。这种动态适应能力对量化交易策略中的市场状态切换（如波动率变化、趋势逆转）具有实用价值，可应用于动量策略调整和风险控制。该方法在模拟测试中优于现有算法，展现了在非平稳金融数据环境下的应用潜力。

title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential for time series reasoning, while models that reason over time series are usually with long chains of thought. However, this process often consumes thousands of tokens, directly leading to substantial latency during inference. In contrast, System 1 models such as Jev make decisions instantly and can naturally be an alternative, but raw time series are not compatible with the embedding space of these models, thus hindering the reasoning performance, especially when input series contain thousands of numeric points. In this paper, we make a very early attempt to propose a time series System 1 model, namely TimesJev. Specifically, we first formalize System 1 sufficiency in time series reasoning, which motivates a compressed representation for time series with key frequency patterns preserved. To construct this representation, we derive a dimension reduction objective that combines (i) a sufficiency divergence that measures the core information lost during compression, and (ii) a realizability divergence that quantifies the incompatibility of the System 1 model to the optimal prediction given this representation. We optimize this objective by learning time series compression with a gating mechanism for sufficiency, and then aligning the selected representation with the embedding space for realizability. Finally, experiments on 13 datasets demonstrate that TimesJev outperforms reasoning models by over 62% with 62.9% less inference time than their fine-tuned versions on average.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TimesJev, a System 1 model for time series reasoning that focuses on compressed representation with key frequency patterns preserved. It uses a dimension reduction objective combining sufficiency divergence and realizability divergence, optimized via a gating mechanism for sufficiency and alignment with the embedding space.
data_sources: The paper experiments on 13 datasets, which likely include time series data, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned. The methodology is general and applicable to any time series data, including financial time series.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to process time series data with high efficiency and reduced latency could be valuable for high-frequency trading or real-time market signal processing. The compressed representation might help in identifying key market patterns quickly, potentially leading to actionable trading signals.
title_cn: TimesJev：快速思考时间序列中的系统1充分性
summary_cn: 该论文提出了TimesJev模型，一种针对时间序列的高效推理方法，通过压缩表示和保留关键频率模式，显著提高推理速度。此技术在金融时间序列（如高频交易数据）处理中具有潜在应用价值，能够快速识别市场模式并生成交易信号。

title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
summary: Trading discipline often fails people. Our study tested whether four AI trading agents followed their strategies and risk rules. Offering traders the evidence and an agent evaluation toolkit to separate luck from following the rules, before giving agents meaningful autonomy or capital. Our study analysed 2,627 closed positions from 12 February to 27 August 2026 across the same asset universe and execution conditions. Most positions were simulated against live prices with a 0.09% round-trip fee; 18% involved real Hyperliquid orders. Each position declared a strategy, stop and target, with a limit of five open positions per agent. The fleet finished net positive after fees. Rule adherence was high across all four agents, including the unprofitable one. Profitability tracked how often agents won relative to their break-even win rates.
