We also establish lower bounds for scalar Gaussian models, showing that, under specified conditions, a suitably chosen constant stepsize achieves the smallest possible worst-case cumulative error up to constant factors, even compared with estimators that use future observations. These results further quantify the effect of temporal correlation on estimation accuracy. Since choosing an appropriate stepsize generally requires knowledge of the noise level and how much the fixed points change, we develop an adaptive method that uses an additional bounded, unbiased observation of the fixed point to achieve an almost optimal algorithm without needing the knowledge of the noise level and the fixed point variation over time. Finally, we apply our results to value-function estimation using synchronous tabular temporal-difference learning in changing environments, assuming generative-model access and a common invariant distribution.
core_methodology: Linear stochastic approximation (SA) with time-varying affine operators to track drifting fixed points under noisy observations
data_sources: Generic noisy observations (not financial-specific); applications tested with temporal-difference learning in changing environments
alpha_potential: Potential application in adapting trading models to non-stationary markets (e.g., regime shifts), but requires significant financial domain adaptation
title_cn: 漂移仿射不动点的随机跟踪方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种时变线性随机逼近方法，用于在噪声观测下跟踪漂移的不动点。对于量化交易，其自适应步骤机制可用于调整策略参数以适应市场机制转换，尤其在处理动量因子衰减或市场微观结构变化时可能具有应用价值。

title: Cognitively Decoupled Meta-Induction for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
summary: In-context learning (ICL) tackles downstream tasks conditioned on demonstrations. This paradigm relies heavily on neighbor-based matching between queries and demonstrations, limiting out-of-distribution (OOD) performance. For better generalization, rule-based inductive reasoning derives task-level regularities, which we term task-level inductive representations (TIR), before directly answering. However, existing methods lack generalizable inductive ability across diverse tasks. Inspired by meta-learning, we propose Cognitive-Decoupling meta-Induction (CoDI) for TIR-based inductive reasoning on general tasks. CoDI comprises a Cognitive-Decoupling Framework for query-blind TIR induction, and a Dual-Loop Meta-Inductive Learning method for cross-task inducer optimization. Empirically, CoDI achieves substantial performance gains on five ID and OOD benchmarks, and preserves OOD gains without explicit induction at inference. Code is available at https://github.com/Yuqian-Wang2277/codi-meta-induction.
core_methodology: Cognitive-Decoupling meta-Induction (CoDI) framework for out-of-distribution generalization through task-level inductive representations and dual-loop meta-learning
data_sources: Not specified (implies potentially any tabular/text data suitable for meta-learning tasks)
alpha_potential: Could potentially improve robustness of AI-based trading strategies when market regimes change (OOD scenarios), though not a direct trading signal generator
title_cn: 认知解耦元归纳用于分布外泛化
summary_cn: 该论文提出的CoDI框架通过任务级归纳表示和双重循环元学习提升模型在分布外场景的表现。在量化交易中，可增强策略在不同市场周期中的适应性，但需结合具体交易信号模型实现直接应用。

title: Remember Less, Adapt Longer: Bounded-State In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Recurrent Summary Memory
summary: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) enables agents to adapt to new tasks without parameter updates, relying on memory to retain what they learn from experience. For agents operating continually, existing approaches using memory trade off bounded cost against access to past experience. Approaches using growing memories, such as full-history attention and accumulating summaries, incur storage and per-decision costs that increase with task length. Fixed-size memories bound storage but restrict access: sliding windows discard older steps, while recurrent networks compress even recent interactions into a hidden state. We introduce Recurrent Summary Memory (RSM), a Transformer policy that attends exactly to a short working buffer of recent interactions and carries a fixed-capacity summary of earlier experience. When the buffer fills, RSM rewrites the summary from its previous contents and the buffer, then clears the buffer, so deployment memory and per-decision cost stay $O(1)$ in task length. On long-running partially observable tasks, frozen RSM policies sustain their adapted performance for eight times the training horizon with about 1% of full-history memory, ending ahead of every evaluated baseline while growing memories deteriorate. When the task configuration changes mid-run, RSM re-adapts better than growing and recurrent memories. Clearing the summary or blocking the policy's access to it removes its benefit, while swapping in another task's summary steers behaviour towards that task. Together, these results show that our fixed-capacity summary can sustain in-context adaptation far beyond the training horizon.
core_methodology: Recurrent Summary Memory (RSM) for in-context reinforcement learning with fixed-capacity memory management
data_sources: Not specified in abstract, but methodology suggests potential application to sequential financial data (e.g., price series, order flow)
alpha_potential: Could potentially enhance adaptive trading strategies in non-stationary markets by maintaining efficient memory of relevant patterns while discarding noise

title: ActTime: Action-Conditioned World Modeling for Time Series
summary: Time-series models increasingly condition on known future inputs. In controlled systems, some of these inputs are actions that can be changed, compared, and optimized before execution. A model must therefore do more than predict the realized future: it must predict how outcomes change under different actions from the same observed history and support reliable comparison of candidate plans. We introduce ActTime, an action-conditioned world model for time series. Over the observed history, ActTime updates variable-specific latent states through an action-conditioned transition and corrects them using observations. It then rolls the same transition forward under candidate actions to generate future trajectories. Training uses only factual trajectories, without paired alternative-action outcomes or planning supervision. We construct a simulator-grounded evaluation suite across building energy, traffic, greenhouse climate, and inventory management, covering factual prediction, intervention-effect prediction, offline decision making, and closed-loop planning. ActTime ranks first in 12 of 16 domain-task settings. Across eight methods, the mean pairwise model-ranking reversal rate is 17.8% between factual prediction and intervention fidelity, and rises to 28.4% between intervention fidelity and decision ranking. These results show that factual accuracy, intervention fidelity, and decision quality are related but not interchangeable.
core_methodology: Action-conditioned world modeling for time series, utilizing variable-specific latent states updated through action-conditioned transitions and corrected with observations, capable of rolling forward candidate actions to generate future trajectories.
data_sources: Potential to be applied to market data, particularly time-series data akin to building energy, traffic, greenhouse climate, and inventory management mentioned in the paper.
alpha_potential: Possible adaptation to predictive modeling of market reactions under different scenarios (e.g., policy changes, corporate actions), potentially uncovering trading signals by comparing outcomes under varying conditions.
title_cn: ActTime：基于动作条件的时间序列世界模型
summary_cn: ActTime是一种基于动作条件的世界模型，适用于时间序列预测。该模型通过动作条件下的状态转换和观测校正生成未来轨迹，可能在金融市场中用于政策变化或事件影响的预测，从而辅助交易决策。

title: Out-of-Distribution Detection in Continual Learning
summary: Out-of-distribution detection in continual learning (OOD-CL) is highly challenging, as it requires (i) learning a sequence of tasks without catastrophic forgetting, and (ii) identifying unknown samples (OOD) without access to known (in-distribution (ID)) data from past tasks, where standard confidence-based OOD scores tend to degrade. Existing methods largely rely on a rehearsal buffer of past data or assume closed-world settings, limiting their scalability and reliability in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel OOD detection framework for rehearsal-free continual learning, inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), which mitigate catastrophic forgetting via their inherent local neuroplasticity. To better leverage KAN in OOD-CL, we introduce a task-adaptive classifier architecture, TA-KAN, which mitigates recency bias and enhances ID--OOD separability through task-specific control of activation locality. Furthermore, we propose a geometry-guided OOD score that complements TA-KAN classifier confidence without relying on past ID data. Our method significantly improves OOD detection while maintaining strong ID classification performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in OOD-CL.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection framework for continual learning, leveraging Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) with a task-adaptive classifier (TA-KAN) and a geometry-guided OOD score. This approach addresses catastrophic forgetting and enhances ID-OOD separability without relying on past data.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but the methodology is applicable to any sequential data, making it potentially useful for financial time series or market regime detection.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for detecting regime changes or anomalies in financial markets, potentially identifying market states where traditional models fail. The OOD detection could signal regime shifts or emerging risks.
title_cn: 持续学习中的分布外检测
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种持续学习中的新型分布外检测框架，通过任务自适应KAN分类器和几何引导的OOD评分，无需依赖历史数据即可有效识别未知样本。该方法可用于金融市场中的状态变化检测和异常识别，可能有助捕捉市场转折点或模型失效场景。

title: LEAPS: Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern Learning and State Tracking
summary: Long-context language models (LCLMs) power agents that act over long trajectories, from improving a codebase to running research experiments to forecasters that condition on lengthy histories. These applications draw on three distinct long-context capabilities: recall, where the answer is a fact present in the context; state tracking, where the outcome can be computed by performing a series of transformations to a specified state; and pattern learning, where the goal is to make a prediction by sampling from a distribution inferred from many observations. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on the first capability. In this work, we introduce LEAPS (Long-context Evaluation of Adaptive Pattern learning and State tracking), a collection of 12 novel datasets, spanning agentic workflows, behavioral modeling, and forecasting of market and world events. By construction, LEAPS is resistant to data contamination, extends to millions of input tokens, and uses reliable metrics. We evaluate 30 API and open models from 8K to 512K input tokens. LEAPS distinguishes models that perform near perfectly on recall tasks, finding that such models' state tracking and pattern learning abilities can vary significantly and degrade much more dramatically with increasing input lengths--even for pattern learning, where more observations should make learning a theoretically easier task. Moreover, thinking models often underperform their base counterparts, exhausting their generation budget or oversimplifying the task. We hope LEAPS can guide the development of the next generation of LCLMs.
core_methodology: Evaluation framework for long-context language models focusing on state tracking and pattern learning capabilities
data_sources: Novel datasets spanning agentic workflows, behavioral modeling, and forecasting of market events
alpha_potential: Potential application in forecasting market events using pattern learning from lengthy historical data, though not directly demonstrated
title_cn: LEAPS：自适应模式学习与状态追踪的长期上下文评估
summary_cn: 本研究提出了LEAPS评估框架，专门测试大型语言模型在状态追踪和模式学习方面的能力，包含12个新型数据集，可延伸至数百万输入标记。虽然在金融领域直接应用尚需验证，但其模式学习能力可能为市场事件预测提供新的技术路径。

title: FinHopper: A Progressive Multi-Hop Benchmark for Complex Financial Agents with Step-wise Evaluation
summary: Financial agents are expected to answer factual investment queries through open search, but financial multi-hop retrieval differs from general multi-hop QA in a crucial way: each intermediate answer is an exact typed constraint, such as an entity, date, event, or numerical indicator, that determines the next query. This strict answer-conditioned dependency makes small intermediate errors cascade into plausible but wrong search trajectories. We introduce FinHopper, a benchmark for complex financial agents with controlled reasoning depth from 1 to 6 hops, covering stocks, funds, and macroeconomic facts, with gold intermediate answers for process-level evaluation. To construct FinHopper at scale, we design a state-transition-based synthesis framework that composes verified atomic financial QA patterns into dependency-preserving chains, followed by targeted in-synthesis verification, model-ensemble checking, and public-search validation by financial experts. Experiments with 20 LLM-agent configurations show that public search tools are necessary but insufficient: performance drops sharply as hop depth increases, the best model remains far below human experts, and process-aware scoring reveals partial reasoning progress hidden by final-answer-only evaluation. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/justajustin/FinHopper/.
core_methodology: Multi-hop retrieval benchmark for financial agents with step-wise evaluation using state-transition-based synthesis framework
data_sources: Stocks, funds, and macroeconomic facts
alpha_potential: Potential to improve accuracy of multi-step financial information retrieval, which could support better investment decisions and reduce error cascades in financial queries

title: FinSafeGuard: A Quality-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Financial AI Safety
summary: Generating high-quality synthetic datasets at scale remains a fundamental challenge for training specialized AI systems in data-scarce domains. We present a comprehensive methodology that produces 14.3 million quality-filtered synthetic training examples from a structured taxonomy of 632,000 scenario specifications. Our four-stage pipeline ad- dresses critical challenges in synthetic data quality, diversity, and realism through: (1) systematic pre-generation research establishing optimal generation parameters via diminishing returns analysis, (2) conditional auto evolution mechanisms that remediate low-diversity batches during generation, (3) a two-layer semantic deduplication architecture combining lexical and embedding-based methods, and (4) LLM-as-Judge quality evaluation filtering samples based on behavioral correctness and tuple fidelity. Empirical analysis across three domains (Banking, Insurance, Financial Services) demonstrates domain-specific deduplication patterns ranging from 9.9% to 40.6%, with output generation modes exhibiting highest redundancy. Our batch size optimization reveals mode-specific diversity saturation thresholds, enabling principled allocation strategies. The complete pipeline reduces 26.4M raw samples to 14.3M high-confidence examples through merge (20.9% reduction), semantic deduplication (18.7% reduction), and quality-based filtering (15.9% reduction), providing a reproducible framework for domain-specific synthetic data generation with rigorous quality control.
core_methodology: The paper presents a four-stage pipeline for generating high-quality synthetic financial data, including systematic pre-generation research, conditional auto evolution mechanisms, semantic deduplication architecture, and LLM-as-Judge quality evaluation. The methodology focuses on improving data quality, diversity, and realism for financial domains.
data_sources: Synthetic data generated from a structured taxonomy of 632,000 scenario specifications across Banking, Insurance, and Financial Services domains.
alpha_potential: The synthetic data generation framework could potentially be used to augment training datasets for AI models in quantitative finance, particularly in areas where real data is scarce. However, the direct application to trading strategies is not explicitly demonstrated in the abstract.
title_cn: FinSafeGuard：一种质量驱动的金融AI安全合成数据集
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种四阶段的合成数据生成框架，专注于提升金融领域AI训练数据的质量、多样性和真实性。虽然不直接涉及交易策略，但其高质量合成数据生成方法可能为金融AI模型的训练提供有价值的数据增强手段。

title: From Retrieval to Recognition:Knowledge-Enhanced Post-training of Time Series Foundation Models for Classification
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) have achieved notable progress in classification tasks through large-scale pretraining. However, their post-training practice mainly focuses on implicit parameter fine-tuning, where task-relevant information is entangled with abundant irrelevant knowledge in vast parameter spaces. This may hinder TSFMs from precisely activating useful knowledge for downstream classification. To this end, we propose Retrieval-to-Recognition (R2R), a plug-and-play post-training paradigm that adapts pretrained TSFMs to time series classification. Rather than pretraining a new foundation model, R2R improves how existing TSFMs are post-trained: it introduces a decoupled query encoder to extract discriminative patterns and retrieve instance-level numerical knowledge from a constructed knowledge base. The retrieved explicit knowledge is then fused with the TSFM's implicit parametric embeddings, enabling joint knowledge transfer at both the parameter and feature levels. In this way, R2R allows TSFMs to recall task-relevant patterns learned during pretraining, improving the efficiency of knowledge utilization in downstream classification transfer. Experiments on 158 time series datasets show that R2R consistently improves the classification performance of state-of-the-art TSFMs. Ablation and knowledge-enhanced studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
core_methodology: A retrieval-based post-training approach for Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) that combines explicit knowledge retrieval with implicit parametric embeddings to enhance classification performance
data_sources: 158 time series datasets (unspecified domain - requires adaptation to financial time series)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve time series classification in financial data (e.g., regime detection, pattern recognition), though not directly tested on market data. The knowledge retrieval mechanism could help identify market regimes or anomaly patterns more efficiently
title_cn: 从检索到识别：时间序列基础模型的分类任务知识增强型后训练方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出的R2R框架通过结合知识检索与参数嵌入，改进了时间序列基础模型在分类任务中的表现。对于量化交易，该方法可能优化金融时间序列的模式识别（如市场状态分类、异常检测），但需针对市场数据专门适配

title: Variance-Aware Non-Stationary Bandits:All-Budget Regret Bounds and Adaptation Costs
summary: Low reward variance reduces estimation cost, but does not eliminate monitoring of arms that may improve while unobserved. We refine the variance--variation tradeoff and characterize how both costs depend on supplied variance and variation budgets in bounded, non-stationary multi-armed bandits. Let $A$ be the number of arms, $T$ the horizon, $B$ a bound on consecutive mean variation excluding the initial vector, and $Q$ a bound on the sum of the largest per-round reward variances. For every admissible pair $Q,B$, the minimax expected dynamic regret is, within a single logarithmic factor, \[ \min\{T,\;A+\sqrt{AQ}+(AQBT)^{1/3} +\sqrt{AT}\min\{B,\sqrt B\}\}. \] The deterministic boundary $Q=0$ is characterized without logarithms. For small positive budgets, a safe calibration phase identifies a common interval containing all future means of surviving arms. Clipping observations to a wider interval reduces the cost of restarting a prior hybrid static-regret algorithm; an original-mean analytical reference controls its residuals without charging the variation of clipped means. Balancing clipping bias and monitoring closes the small-budget noisy regime. Fixed oblivious constructions give the matching lower bound. We also quantify adaptation costs: on a disclosed deterministic one-improvement family, a stationary-regret budget has a matching worst-case change-regret frontier, including a finite improvement pulse. This implies an $\Omega((T/A)^{1/4})$ loss when one policy competes with all supplied-budget deterministic oracle rates. The budget-free low-noise scheduling problem remains separate.
core_methodology: Non-stationary multi-armed bandits with variance-awareness for dynamic regret minimization under bounded variation and variance budgets
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any sequential decision-making problem with non-stationary rewards (could be mapped to asset returns)
alpha_potential: Potential for adaptive portfolio allocation in changing market regimes by optimally balancing exploration/exploitation under reward uncertainty
title_cn: 方差感知的非平稳多臂老虎机：全预算后悔界与适应成本
summary_cn: 该研究提出了方差感知的非平稳多臂老虎机框架，通过创新地平衡方差-变化权衡关系，可为量化交易中动态资产配置提供理论支持。其核心在于根据市场波动程度调整探索策略，特别适合处理市场状态变化时的投资组合优化问题。

title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Capability-Focused Evaluation with Structural Diversity for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Static public benchmarks for time series foundation models (TSFMs) typically have fixed and narrow test distributions. Their repeated reuse encourages benchmark-specific tuning, making reported performance reflect adaptation to the fixed test set rather than genuine forecasting generalization. In addition, a single aggregate score cannot fully characterize model capabilities across distinct temporal structures and input relationships. We propose CaFE (Capability-Focused Evaluation), a refreshable evaluation extension grounded in original benchmark data that enriches static benchmarks with structural diversity and enriches single-score black-box evaluation with multi-dimensional, capability-oriented assessment. CaFE first profiles the original benchmark and defines eight Structural Features (SFs) that characterize its temporal structure. For each SF, it resamples the original data according to its structural support, removes edge-of-distribution samples, and augments the retained samples by varying the SF's salience, producing samples with different structural profiles. After filtering out out-of-distribution samples while preserving diversity, CaFE yields a refreshed evaluation set. TSFMs are then evaluated on this set using both conventional forecast-error metrics and intervention-response metrics, giving each model a per-feature capability profile alongside endpoint accuracy. Experiments on GIFT-Eval and FEV-Mini20 show that CaFE yields stable evaluation results and reveals per-feature strengths and weaknesses that a single aggregate score hides. Moreover, on genuine data filtered by structural condition, models selected by CaFE outperform those chosen by the aggregate leaderboard. CaFE therefore makes model selection conditional on the structural response of interest.
core_methodology: CaFE introduces a capability-focused evaluation framework for time series foundation models (TSFMs) by enriching static benchmarks with structural diversity and multi-dimensional assessment. It defines eight Structural Features (SFs), resamples data to vary SF salience, and evaluates models using both forecast-error metrics and intervention-response metrics.
data_sources: The paper uses original benchmark data from GIFT-Eval and FEV-Mini20, which are presumably time series datasets, though specific market data is not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The methodology could help in selecting better time series models for financial forecasting by identifying per-feature strengths and weaknesses, potentially leading to more robust trading signals. However, direct alpha generation is not demonstrated and would require adaptation to financial data.
title_cn: 超越静态排行榜：基于结构多样性的时间序列基础模型能力评估
summary_cn: CaFE框架通过引入结构多样性和多维评估，改进了时间序列基础模型的评估方法。它能识别模型在不同时间结构特征上的表现，有助于选择更稳健的金融预测模型，但需针对市场数据进行专门优化以产生实际交易优势。

title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
summary: Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.
core_methodology: Recursive Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that learns iterative solution procedures for Second-Order Cone Programs (SOCPs), leveraging solver trajectories to progressively refine estimates
data_sources: Standard SOCP problem classes (not financial-specific but methodologically transferable)
alpha_potential: Potential to accelerate portfolio optimization, risk management calculations, and other convex optimization problems in finance through hybrid solver approaches (warm-starting traditional methods)
title_cn: 基于图神经网络的SOCP求解器动力学学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出的SOCPNet框架通过递归图神经网络学习二阶锥规划问题的迭代求解过程，可用于加速投资组合优化等金融领域的凸优化计算。该方法通过混合求解策略（预启动传统内点法）在保持精度的同时减少计算成本。

title: Toward Online Robust Zero-Sum Markov Games with Function Approximation
summary: Online robust zero-sum Markov games pose a coupled operator-learning and game-solving problem: from nominal interaction data, the learner must recover a worst-case minimax Bellman operator while maintaining strategic coverage and controlling stage-game approximation error. Existing robust reinforcement-learning theory does not yet provide such an operator-learning perspective beyond specialized multi-agent settings. We develop an optimistic dual robust Bellman framework that combines dual robust Bellman fitting, optimistic minimax planning, backward-validated confidence sets, and exploiter-mix data collection. Our analysis is organized around the robust Bellman residuals induced by the candidate value class and yields a regret reduction that separates exploration complexity, robust operator-estimation error, stage-game solution error, and misspecification. Under explicit interpretable assumptions, we obtain conditional theorem interfaces for general and projected function approximation, together with closed results in several structured regimes, including tabular, epochwise cross-fit linear, self-normalized pure-online linear / finite-rank kernel, and projected RKHS truncation. Small-scale numerical experiments illustrate robustness calibration, strategic coverage, and the return-gap trade-off predicted by the framework.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an optimistic dual robust Bellman framework combining dual robust Bellman fitting, optimistic minimax planning, and exploiter-mix data collection for online robust zero-sum Markov games. It focuses on separating exploration complexity, robust operator-estimation error, stage-game solution error, and misspecification.
data_sources: Nominal interaction data (likely simulated or abstract game scenarios), though the methodology could theoretically be applied to financial market data.
alpha_potential: The framework could potentially be adapted to model adversarial market conditions or develop robust trading strategies that account for worst-case scenarios. The method's focus on minimax optimization and robustness may help in designing strategies resilient to market regime changes.
title_cn: 面向在线鲁棒零和马尔科夫博弈的函数逼近方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种结合双鲁棒贝尔曼拟合和乐观极小化规划的框架，适用于在线零和马尔科夫博弈。该方法通过分离探索复杂度、算子估计误差和博弈求解误差，为金融市场的对抗性环境建模提供了理论工具，可潜在用于开发适应市场状态变化的鲁棒交易策略。

title: A Simple and General Approach to top-$k$ Selection
summary: This paper considers the Bayesian top-$k$ identification problem, wherein a decision maker is tasked with selecting $k$ items from a pool of items of unknown quality. To assess the items, the decision maker adaptively allocates a fixed sampling budget, where each sample of an item yields a noisy observation of its quality, with the objective of minimizing the expected opportunity cost of the selected set. We propose an approach that allocates each batch of samples by minimizing a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on the expected opportunity cost. The approach is general: samples can be allocated in batches, the selection size $k$ is arbitrary, and it applies to many sampling distributions. It is also simple and intuitive. We prove that the method's posterior expected opportunity cost decays at an exponential rate of at least half the best rate achievable by any sampling rule. In simulations across a wide range of settings, the method is competitive with, and often improves upon, the best existing algorithm in each setting.
core_methodology: Bayesian top-k identification problem solving through adaptive sampling to minimize expected opportunity cost of selected items. Uses batch sampling with a surrogate objective based on upper bound of opportunity cost.
data_sources: General noisy quality observations of items - could be adapted to any financial data stream where quality assessment is required (e.g., stocks, factors, trading signals)
alpha_potential: Potential application in factor selection, optimal portfolio construction, or signal aggregation where limited sampling budget exists. Could help identify the top-k best performing assets/strategies efficiently.
title_cn: 一种通用且简单的top-k选择方法
summary_cn: 本文提出一种贝叶斯方法来高效识别最优top-k项（如资产或因子），通过自适应采样最小化机会成本。在量化交易中，可应用于因子筛选、组合优化等场景，特别适合有采样限制的情况。

title: Reward Objectives for Robust (PO)MDPs: A Law-Preserving Equivalence with (Partially Observable) Games
summary: Robust partially observable Markov decision processes model agents that act under partial observability while adversarial environment resolves uncertainty in the transition probabilities. Reward objectives such as discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward under finite and infinite horizons allow quantifying the utility of an agent. We consider the problem of solving RPOMDPs under all four reward objectives, where the goal is to decide whether the value of a risk measure with respect to a reward objective exceeds a given threshold. We consider different risk measures, such as (1)~expected value, (2)~mean-variance (MV), (3)~conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), and (4)~entropic risk (ERisk). Our results can be summarized as follows. First, we formalize the class of law-invariant risk measures, that subsume all four risk measures above. Second, we propose a unified framework for solving RPOMDPs with discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward objectives under any law-invariant risk measure, by reducing the problem to solving partially observable stochastic games (POSGs). Our unified framework applies to (s,a)-rectangular RPOMDPs with polytopic uncertainty sets, which we show to be {\em equivalent} to POSGs, for each of the four reward objectives and any law-invariant risk measure. We prove equivalence by designing logspace reductions between the RPOMDP and POSG models, that map strategies to strategies and preserve the distribution of the reward objective, up to a constant rescaling factor. Third, as a corollary, we derive new computational complexity results for R(PO)MDPs and POSGs. In particular, we show that solving (s,a)-rectangular RMDPs is as hard as solving simple stochastic games.
core_methodology: The paper presents a unified framework for solving Robust Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (RPOMDPs) under various reward objectives and risk measures, including expected value, mean-variance, conditional value-at-risk, and entropic risk. The approach reduces the problem to solving Partially Observable Stochastic Games (POSGs) and establishes equivalence between the models.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but focuses on theoretical models (RPOMDPs and POSGs) with polytopic uncertainty sets and adversarial environments.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to model and optimize trading strategies under uncertainty and adversarial conditions, potentially improving risk-adjusted returns by incorporating robust decision-making under partial observability.
title_cn: 鲁棒（部分可观测）马尔可夫决策过程的奖励目标：与（部分可观测）博弈的保持律等价性
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种统一的框架，用于在部分可观测和对抗环境下解决鲁棒马尔可夫决策过程中的多种奖励目标和风险度量问题。通过将其转化为部分可观测随机博弈，该方法为在金融市场不确定性和部分信息条件下优化交易策略提供了理论基础，尤其在风险管理和鲁棒投资组合优化方面具有潜在应用价值。

title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
summary: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. This enables scenario analysis: forecasting how a target responds to events that set covariates to chosen future values. Whether they can do this reliably is an open question. We introduce WhatIf-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well forecasters use covariates to forecast a target's response to future events. WhatIf-Bench is semi-synthetic: time series come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks, with controlled covariate-target relationships grounded in each system. Each task presents a history of events intervening on covariates, then asks to forecast a future event that either replays seen values (Replay) or sets them to unseen ones (Novel). Varying the number of covariates, historical events, and event length yields 37,665 tasks. Evaluating TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and simple regression baselines, we find the LLMs reach the highest skill (improvement over a naive baseline), ahead of the best TSFMs. Every model forecasts well on Replay futures (48 to 85% skill) but drops to -7 to 50% on Novel futures, with the regression baselines falling the most. Skill on Novel futures also falls as events set more covariates jointly. More historical events raise skill on Novel futures across the board, but large differences remain. WhatIf-Bench reveals generalization to Novel futures as the core challenge, and offers a testbed toward arbitrary scenario analysis.
core_methodology: Benchmarking intervention-aware time series forecasting using semi-synthetic data from mechanistic simulators to evaluate how well models forecast responses to future events.
data_sources: Semi-synthetic time series from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to assess the impact of macroeconomic or company-specific events on financial time series, providing a framework for scenario analysis in trading strategies.
title_cn: WhatIf-Bench：干预感知时间序列预测的基准测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基准测试方法，评估模型在时间序列预测中对未来干预事件的响应能力。通过半合成数据模拟不同系统（如数据中心、电网等），测试模型在重复事件和新事件下的表现。这一方法可扩展至金融领域，用于分析宏观或公司事件对市场数据的影响，为交易策略中的情景分析提供框架。

title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
summary: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. We validate our proposed offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework on an industry case study involving rideshare coupon targeting, where customer states are defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. We evaluate performance using model-based off-policy evaluation, with causal dynamics estimated from a temporal holdout. Under the observed coupon budget and RFM state representation, our optimized policy improves customer lifetime value (LTV) by 19% over the estimated behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline. Although the demonstrated action space is binary, the proposed framework is action-agnostic, yielding a general-purpose decision module for targeting systems that manage multiple interventions.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) integrated with off-policy causal correction via Linear Programming (LP) to optimize long-term value while satisfying operational constraints. This approach is validated using offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) with causal dynamics estimation.
data_sources: The case study uses rideshare coupon targeting data, with customer states defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. However, the methodology is action-agnostic and could theoretically be applied to financial data.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to optimize long-term value under constraints could be adapted for portfolio optimization or algorithmic trading strategies that require balancing multiple objectives (e.g., risk, return, transaction costs). The causal correction aspect may help address market regime changes.
title_cn: 最佳下一步行动：基于因果约束离线强化学习的商业行动目标优化
summary_cn: 该论文提出的因果约束离线强化学习框架，通过线性规划整合因果校正，可在满足业务约束条件下优化长期价值。虽应用于商业场景，但其方法论对量化交易中的多目标策略优化（如平衡收益与风险）具有潜在借鉴价值。

title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
summary: Long-horizon agents must learn heterogeneous capabilities from interleaved trajectories. Updating shared parameters to learn new capabilities can degrade previously acquired ones, resulting in catastrophic forgetting. As a trajectory unfolds, different stages may require different capabilities, yet conventional joint training and static adapter merging maintain a fixed parameter configuration throughout execution. We introduce WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions), which trains independent capability-specific LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone and adds adapter selection to the agent's action space. These internal actions use the model's native tool-calling interface for on-demand capability composition in a shared context. Across eight deep-research benchmarks, Qwen3-32B with WeAct improves average accuracy by 6.2% relative to full fine-tuning counterparts despite using less compute, and by 27.5% relative to the strongest static LoRA-merging method. WeAct also supports modular continual adaptation, by adding a new code computation adapter to expand the agent's capabilities and updating the existing writing adapter to improve report quality. Both updates leave the backbone and other adapters unchanged, supporting modular continual adaptation in agents.
core_methodology: The paper introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions), a method for dynamic weight switching in agents using LoRA adapters to prevent catastrophic forgetting and enable modular continual adaptation. This approach allows for on-demand capability composition within a shared context, improving accuracy and efficiency.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on deep-research benchmarks, which could be adapted to financial datasets for agent-based trading systems.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to develop adaptive trading agents that dynamically switch between different trading strategies or factors based on market conditions, potentially capturing alpha by leveraging heterogeneous capabilities without forgetting previous strategies.
title_cn: WeAct：动态权重切换作为智能体动作
summary_cn: WeAct提出了一种动态权重切换方法，通过LoRA适配器防止灾难性遗忘，支持模块化持续适应。该方法可应用于构建自适应交易智能体，动态切换不同交易策略，有望在多变市场条件下捕捉阿尔法。

title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes
summary: Cox processes provide a principled Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling event-based data through an underlying intensity function. However, existing inference methods for estimating the intensity typically rely on computationally expensive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling or approximate inference techniques. In addition, to ensure tractability, these methods often define priors over indirect latent structures, making them challenging to interpret. In this paper, we introduce the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), which recasts Bayesian intensity estimation as inference over unobserved events given the observed event history. This perspective avoids the need to define complex priors while retaining the flexibility of nonparametric modeling. We propose a scalable, GPU-friendly copula-based predictive update, and provide strong theoretical guarantees for the convergence of the predictive resampling algorithm. Empirically, we show that MPCP provides excellent performance in both simulations and real data at a fraction of the computational cost of competing Bayesian approaches.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), a Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling event-based data through an underlying intensity function. It avoids complex priors and uses a scalable, GPU-friendly copula-based predictive update for inference.
data_sources: The methodology is applicable to event-based data, which in finance could include trade executions, order book events, or news arrivals.
alpha_potential: The MPCP could be used to model and predict rare events or high-frequency trading signals, potentially uncovering inefficiencies in event-driven markets.
title_cn: 鞅后验Cox过程
summary_cn: 本文提出了鞅后验Cox过程（MPCP），通过贝叶斯非参数方法建模事件数据，避免了复杂先验并采用可扩展的GPU友好型Copula预测更新。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于高频交易信号或罕见事件预测，具有潜在的阿尔法发现能力。

title: Towards instance-dependent regret optimality in Episodic MDPs with Posterior Sampling
summary: We study regret minimization in finite-horizon episodic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). While minimax-optimal algorithms are known, tractable approaches to instance-dependent optimality are still lacking. Motivated by this gap, we introduce $\pi_0$-PSRL, a variant of PSRL that uses posterior samples to decide when exploration is needed, while following a fixed reference policy $\pi_0$ during exploration episodes. This decouples the test for exploration, triggered when the sampled and empirical MDPs have different optimal policies, from the choice of the policy used to gather information. The resulting design addresses a limitation of standard PSRL, where the sampled optimal policy may not be the optimal choice for exploration. We prove instance-dependent regret bounds for $\pi_0$-PSRL, identifying the logarithmic exploration cost induced by $\pi_0$ and taking a step toward matching asymptotic lower bounds for episodic RL. Our proof techniques showcase a novel proof structure to derive problem-dependent regret bounds in episodic MDPs, and concentration results for Dirichlet random variables, that may be of independent interest.
core_methodology: Introduces π₀-PSRL, a variant of Posterior Sampling for RL that decouples exploration testing from exploitation policy choice using a reference policy π₀. Focuses on instance-dependent optimality in episodic MDPs.
data_sources: Does not specify financial datasets but methodology could be applied to market structure modeling or trading policy optimization.
alpha_potential: Could help optimize exploration-exploitation trade-offs in automated trading systems, particularly in strategy adaptation to changing regimes.
title_cn: 在片段式马尔可夫决策过程中实现基于实例的遗憾最优化的后验采样方法研究
summary_cn: 本文提出的π₀-PSRL算法通过分离探索测试与利用策略选择，改进了标准PSRL在金融交易策略优化中的应用。该方法可用于设计更智能的探索机制，在动态市场环境中实现策略适应性调整，对于高频交易和算法组合管理具有潜在价值。

title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
summary: Bilevel optimization provides a framework for machine learning tasks such as hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning. Existing Newton-based bilevel methods typically rely on the classical hypergradient formula, which is generally unavailable when lower-level solutions are nonunique and the lower-level Hessian is singular. We develop two Newton-based methods beyond lower-level strong convexity by exploiting curvature shared by the lower-level and multiplier updates. Newton-based GALET handles potentially singular lower-level curvature under a positive spectral-gap condition, exploiting its range structure to avoid the squared-Hessian multiplier system used in GALET. Newton-based BAMM uses a strongly convex aggregation model when the lower-level objective is convex and the upper-level objective is strongly convex in the lower-level variable. We establish convergence guarantees and improved complexity bounds relative to GALET and sl-BAMM under the corresponding assumptions. We further introduce GNBO, a generalized Newton-based framework that captures the shared-curvature structure of the proposed methods and several existing Newton and quasi-Newton bilevel methods. Experiments on synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting evaluate the proposed methods across different bilevel learning tasks.
core_methodology: Newton-based methods for bilevel optimization, handling scenarios without lower-level strong convexity or unique solutions, utilizing shared curvature structures between levels.
data_sources: Synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting; tested theoretically for various bilevel learning tasks.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in optimizing hierarchical decision-making processes in trading strategy parameter tuning or meta-learning frameworks where traditional hyperparameter optimization fails.
title_cn: 超越下层强凸性的双层优化牛顿法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了针对双层优化问题的新牛顿法，特别适用于下层解非唯一或Hessian矩阵奇异的情况。在量化交易中，该方法可能改进策略参数优化流程，尤其在处理复杂、非凸的市场模型时展现出潜力。

title: Gradient Boosting Reinforcement Learning
summary: We present Gradient Boosting Reinforcement Learning (GBRL), a framework that adapts the strengths of gradient boosting trees (GBT) to reinforcement learning (RL) tasks. While neural networks (NNs) have become the de facto choice for RL, they face significant challenges with structured and categorical features and tend to generalize poorly to out-of-distribution samples. These are challenges for which GBTs have traditionally excelled in supervised learning. However, GBT's application in RL has been limited. The design of traditional GBT libraries is optimized for static datasets with fixed labels, making them incompatible with RL's dynamic nature, where both state distributions and reward signals evolve during training. GBRL overcomes this limitation by continuously interleaving tree construction with environment interaction. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that GBRL outperforms NNs in domains with structured observations and categorical features while maintaining competitive performance on standard continuous control benchmarks. Like its supervised learning counterpart, GBRL demonstrates superior robustness to out-of-distribution samples and better handles irregular state-action relationships.
core_methodology: GBRL combines gradient boosting trees (GBT) with reinforcement learning (RL) to handle structured and categorical features effectively, addressing issues like poor generalization of neural networks (NNs) in RL tasks.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but implies applicability to domains with structured observations and categorical features, which could include market microstructure data or factor-based datasets.
alpha_potential: GBRL's superior robustness to out-of-distribution samples and better handling of irregular state-action relationships could be leveraged in trading strategies that rely on non-traditional or structured data, offering potential alpha in niche markets or complex trading environments.

title: Risk-averse learning with delayed feedback
summary: In real-world scenarios, risk-averse learning is valuable for mitigating potential adverse outcomes. However, the delayed feedback makes it challenging to assess and manage risk effectively. In this paper, we investigate risk-averse learning using Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) as risk measure, while incorporating feedback with random but bounded delays. We develop two risk-averse learning algorithms that rely on one-point and two-point zeroth-order optimization approaches, respectively. The dynamic regrets of the algorithms are analyzed in terms of the cumulative delay and the number of total samplings. In the absence of delay, the regret bounds match the established bounds of zeroth-order stochastic gradient methods for risk-averse learning. Furthermore, the two-point risk-averse learning outperforms the one-point algorithm by achieving a smaller regret bound. We provide numerical experiments on a dynamic pricing problem to demonstrate the performance of the algorithms.
core_methodology: Risk-averse learning using Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) with one-point and two-point zeroth-order optimization approaches in delayed feedback environments.
data_sources: The paper demonstrates applications on a dynamic pricing problem, suggesting potential use with market pricing data, order book data, or execution data with delayed feedback.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially identify and exploit market inefficiencies by better managing risk in environments with delayed feedback (e.g., execution delays, latency arbitrage scenarios). The two-point approach shows particular promise with smaller regret bounds.
title_cn: 存在延迟反馈的风险规避学习
summary_cn: 本研究针对延迟反馈环境开发了基于条件风险价值(CVaR)的风险规避学习算法，采用零阶优化方法。在动态定价等金融应用中，该算法能有效管理延迟带来的风险，特别是在高频交易、订单执行等存在延迟的场景中具有潜在应用价值。两点优化方法在后悔边界上表现更优。

title: Enhancing Offline Model-Based RL via Active Model Selection: A Bayesian Optimization Perspective
summary: Offline model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) serves as a competitive framework that can learn well-performing policies solely from pre-collected data with the help of learned dynamics models. To fully unleash the power of offline MBRL, model selection plays a pivotal role in determining the dynamics model utilized for downstream policy learning. However, offline MBRL conventionally relies on validation or off-policy evaluation, which are rather inaccurate due to the inherent distribution shift in offline RL. To tackle this, we propose BOMS, an active model selection framework that enhances model selection in offline MBRL with only a small online interaction budget, through the lens of Bayesian optimization (BO). Specifically, we recast model selection as BO and enable probabilistic inference in BOMS by proposing a novel model-induced kernel, which is theoretically grounded and computationally efficient. Through extensive experiments, we show that BOMS improves over the baseline methods with a small amount of online interaction comparable to only $1\%$-$2.5\%$ of offline training data on various RL tasks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces BOMS, an active model selection framework for offline model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) using Bayesian optimization (BO). It proposes a novel model-induced kernel to enhance probabilistic inference and model selection.
data_sources: Pre-collected offline data for reinforcement learning tasks, with a small amount of online interaction (1%-2.5% of offline data).
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for optimizing trading strategies by selecting the best models for market dynamics prediction, potentially improving strategy robustness and performance in varying market conditions.
title_cn: 通过主动模型选择增强离线基于模型的强化学习：贝叶斯优化视角
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种名为BOMS的主动模型选择框架，结合贝叶斯优化来提升离线基于模型的强化学习。该方法仅需少量在线交互即可优化模型选择，可能应用于金融市场的动态预测和交易策略优化，提高模型在分布变化下的鲁棒性。

title: Universal Learning of Nonlinear Dynamics
summary: We study the fundamental problem of one-step prediction of a marginally stable unknown nonlinear dynamical system. We describe an algorithm for this problem, based on the technique of spectral filtering, which learns a mapping from past observations to the next based on a spectral representation of the system. Using techniques from online convex optimization, we prove vanishing prediction error for any nonexpansive nonlinear dynamical system with finitely many marginally stable modes, with rates governed by a novel quantitative control-theoretic notion of learnability. The main technical component of our method is a new spectral filtering algorithm for linear dynamical systems, which incorporates past observations and applies to general noisy and marginally stable systems. This generalizes the original spectral filtering algorithm to both asymmetric dynamics as well as incorporating noise correction, and is of independent interest.
core_methodology: Spectral filtering algorithm for learning nonlinear dynamics, incorporating online convex optimization techniques and noise correction for marginally stable systems
data_sources: Generic time-series data (could potentially be applied to financial time series)
alpha_potential: Potential for predicting short-term market movements or regime shifts in nonlinear financial systems, particularly in mean-reverting or range-bound markets
title_cn: 非线性动态系统的通用学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于谱过滤的算法，用于学习边际稳定的非线性动态系统的一步预测。对于量化交易，这种方法可以应用于市场状态预测和短期价格动态建模，特别是在市场呈现非线性或边际稳定特性时。该方法通过谱表示和在线优化技术实现预测误差的最小化，可能有助于开发新的统计套利或市场状态转换策略。

title: Optimal hypersurface decision trees
summary: Optimal decision trees have attracted increasing attention in recent years, yet existing algorithms face two closely related challenges. First, the trees they construct have limited expressivity because their splitting rules are typically restricted to axis-parallel splits or binary features. Second, these algorithms generally scale poorly to large datasets. These challenges compound one another: more expressive splitting rules increase the combinatorial complexity of the search space, making the resulting optimal decision tree (ODT) problem even more difficult to solve. Building on the proper decision tree framework of \citet{he2025odt}, we propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first algorithm for constructing optimal decision trees with hypersurface splits. The algorithm has worst-case work complexity $O\left(K!K N^{KG+1}\right)$ when $N\geq K$ and fixed-dimensional feasibility tests are treated as constant-cost operations, where $G=\binom{D+M}{M}-1$ depends on the hypersurface polynomial degree $M$ and the data dimension $D$. Its structure is naturally amenable to vectorization and parallelization, enabling efficient execution on GPUs, and the generic algorithm design can be used to accelerate other ODT variants, such as axis-parallel decision (ADT) trees. We further develop a safe pruning strategy that substantially reduces the number of candidate configurations and an incremental generation procedure that reduces the associated feasibility-checking cost from $O(K^2)$ to $O(K)$.
core_methodology: Algorithm for constructing optimal decision trees with hypersurface splits, enhancing expressivity through polynomial degree M and data dimension D. Includes vectorization, parallelization, and pruning strategies for efficiency.
data_sources: Generic, can be applied to any structured financial data (e.g., pricing, volume, technical indicators, fundamental data).
alpha_potential: Potential to uncover non-linear relationships in financial data beyond traditional axis-parallel splits, useful for feature construction and pattern recognition in trading signals.
title_cn: 最优超曲面决策树
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种构建具有超曲面分割的最优决策树的算法，通过多项式度和数据维度增强表达能力，并利用向量化和并行化技术提升效率。在金融领域，该方法可应用于识别价格、成交量等数据中的非线性关系，为交易信号生成和特征构建提供新途径。

title: SPRINT: Stochastic Performative Prediction With Variance Reduction
summary: Performative prediction (PP) is an algorithmic framework for optimizing machine learning (ML) models where the model's deployment affects the distribution of the data it is trained on. Compared to traditional ML with fixed data, designing algorithms in PP converging to a stable point -- known as a stationary performative stable (SPS) solution -- is more challenging than the counterpart in conventional ML tasks due to the model-induced distribution shifts. While considerable efforts have been made to find SPS solutions using methods such as repeated gradient descent (RGD) and greedy stochastic gradient descent (SGD-GD), most prior studies assumed a strongly convex loss until a recent work established $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence of SGD-GD to SPS solutions under smooth, non-convex losses. However, this latest progress is still based on the restricted bounded variance assumption in stochastic gradient estimates and yields convergence bounds with a non-vanishing error neighborhood that scales with the variance. This limitation motivates us to improve convergence rates and reduce error in stochastic optimization for PP, particularly in non-convex settings. Thus, we propose a new algorithm called stochastic performative prediction with variance reduction (SPRINT) and establish its convergence to an SPS solution at a rate of $O(1/T)$. Notably, the resulting error neighborhood is independent of the variance of the stochastic gradients. Experiments on multiple real datasets with non-convex models demonstrate that SPRINT outperforms SGD-GD in both convergence rate and stability.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SPRINT, a stochastic optimization algorithm for performative prediction that reduces variance and improves convergence to stable solutions in non-convex settings. This is particularly relevant for ML models where the model's predictions affect the data distribution they are trained on, a scenario commonly encountered in algorithmic trading.
data_sources: The abstract mentions experiments on multiple real datasets, though specific financial datasets are not detailed. The methodology is general enough to be applied to financial time-series data or other market-related data where model predictions can influence market behavior.
alpha_potential: The algorithm's ability to handle distribution shifts caused by the model's own predictions (performative feedback loops) could be valuable in trading strategies where the act of trading based on model predictions influences market prices, a common issue in high-frequency trading or market-making strategies.
title_cn: SPRINT：具有方差缩减的随机执行预测
summary_cn: SPRINT是一种针对执行预测的随机优化算法，在非凸设置下减少方差并提高收敛稳定性。该算法在处理模型预测影响数据分布的反馈循环方面表现优异，适用于量化交易中因交易行为影响市场价格的情况，如高频交易或做市策略。

title: Interpretable time series analysis with Gumbel dynamics
summary: Switching dynamical systems can model complicated time series data while maintaining interpretability by inferring a finite set of dynamics primitives and explaining different portions of the observed time series with one of these primitives. However, due to the discrete nature of this set, such models struggle to capture smooth, variable-speed transitions, as well as stochastic mixtures of overlapping states (e.g., non-instantaneous state transitions), and the inferred dynamics often display spurious rapid switching on real-world datasets. Here, we propose the Gumbel Dynamical Model (GDM). First, by introducing a continuous relaxation of discrete states and a different noise model defined on the relaxed-discrete state space via the Gumbel distribution, GDM expands the set of available state dynamics, allowing the model to approximate smoother and non-stationary ground-truth dynamics more faithfully. Breaking from established literature, this new class uses a stochastic relaxed state to directly combine reusable dynamical primitives and govern observations, without a separate stochastic continuous trajectory. Second, the relaxation makes the model fully differentiable, enabling fast and scalable training with standard gradient descent methods. We validate our approach on standard simulation datasets and highlight its ability to model soft, sticky states and transitions in a stochastic setting. Furthermore, we apply our model to two real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to infer interpretable states in stochastic time series with multiple dynamics, a setting where traditional methods often fail.
core_methodology: The Gumbel Dynamical Model (GDM) introduces a continuous relaxation of discrete states and a Gumbel distribution-based noise model to enable smoother and non-stationary state transitions in time series analysis. This allows the model to better capture variable-speed transitions and stochastic mixtures of overlapping states, while maintaining interpretability.
data_sources: Standard simulation datasets and two unspecified real-world datasets, likely including stochastic time series with multiple dynamics.
alpha_potential: GDM's ability to infer interpretable states in stochastic time series with multiple dynamics could be useful in identifying regime changes in financial markets, trading patterns, or other market microstructure phenomena. However, direct application to trading strategies would require validation on financial datasets.
title_cn: 基于Gumbel动态模型的可解释时间序列分析
summary_cn: 该研究提出的Gumbel动态模型（GDM）通过引入连续的离散状态松弛和Gumbel分布噪声模型，改进了传统切换动态系统在捕捉平滑、非平稳状态转换方面的不足。对于金融时间序列分析，GDM可用于识别市场中的动态模式转换和状态重叠，可能在识别市场机制变化或交易模式中发挥作用，但其在量化交易中的实际应用仍需进一步验证。

title: $\kappa$-Explorer: Minimax Active Model Estimation in MDPs
summary: Accurately estimating the transition dynamics of an unknown Markov decision process (MDP) is a central problem in reinforcement learning. The accuracy of overall model estimation, however, depends on both the stochasticity of the transitions given state--action pairs, what we call the intrinsic (statistical) complexity of each pair, and the visitation frequency of each state--action pair, dictated extrinsically by the exploration policy and its induced occupancy measure. We propose $\kappa$-Explorer, an active exploration algorithm that constructs an exploration reward for each state--action pair, using a $\kappa$-powered ratio of estimated intrinsic complexity to extrinsic visitation frequency of each pair. By planning with these rewards, $\kappa$-Explorer adapts its extrinsic visitation frequency to the intrinsic complexity of transitions. More specifically, we show that $\kappa$-Explorer optimizes a surrogate objective function which bounds the minimax estimation error. Furthermore, we establish a surrogate objective gap of $\widetilde{O}(t^{-1/3})$, yielding a finite-sample guarantee for sufficiently large $\kappa$. Finally, we extend the framework to alternative estimation losses and objectives beyond the minimax setting.
core_methodology: Active exploration algorithm using a kappa-powered ratio of intrinsic complexity to extrinsic visitation frequency for model estimation in MDPs.
data_sources: Simulated MDP environments; potentially applicable to financial markets with appropriate adaptation.
alpha_potential: Improves model estimation accuracy which could enhance reinforcement learning-based trading strategies by better understanding market dynamics.

title: Topological Compression of Prediction Market Belief States for Event Forecasting
summary: Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and Persistent Homology (PH) have been utilized in numerous fields$-$from protein modeling to financial analysis$-$to understand the underlying structure of data. In this paper, we incorporate TDA and PH into forecasting models over a prediction market universe to determine whether the belief state of such markets forms an underlying structure whose shape can provide predictive insight. We conclude that single-parameter PH is able to improve predictive ability and calibrated accuracy of linear forecasting models, while two-parameter multipersistence produces similar benefits for nonlinear models.
core_methodology: The paper employs Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and Persistent Homology (PH) to analyze the underlying structure of prediction market belief states. It explores single-parameter PH for linear models and two-parameter multipersistence for nonlinear models to enhance forecasting accuracy.
data_sources: Prediction market data, specifically the belief states of participants in such markets.
alpha_potential: The methodology identifies structural patterns in market beliefs that may not be captured by traditional linear or nonlinear models, potentially offering a novel signal source for event forecasting in financial markets.
title_cn: 预测市场信念状态的拓扑压缩用于事件预测
summary_cn: 本研究通过拓扑数据分析和持久同调技术，分析预测市场信念状态的结构特征，发现单参数持久同调可提升线性模型的预测能力，而双参数多重持久同调对非线性模型有类似效果。该方法为金融市场事件预测提供了新的结构信号源。

title: On the utility problem in a market where price impact is transient
summary: We consider a discrete-time model of a financial market where a risky asset is bought and sold with transactions having a transient price impact. It is shown that the corresponding utility maximization problem admits a solution. We manage to remove some unnatural restrictions on the market depth and resilience processes that were present in earlier work. A non-standard feature of the problem is that the set of attainable portfolio values may fail the convexity property.
core_methodology: Discrete-time mathematical modeling of utility maximization in markets with transient price impact
data_sources: Theoretical market model (no specific empirical data mentioned)
alpha_potential: Addresses optimal execution and portfolio construction under realistic market impact conditions, potentially improving transaction cost modeling
title_cn: 论价格冲击具有暂态性的市场中的效用问题
summary_cn: 该研究建立了离散时间金融市场模型，研究在存在暂态价格冲击的情况下效用最大化问题的解决方案。相较于前人工作，其放宽了对市场深度和弹性过程的限制条件，更贴近现实交易环境，可用于优化高频交易或大宗交易的执行策略（尽管模型中投资组合可能呈现非凸特性）。

title: What "Form'' of Uncertainty Does Conformal Prediction Quantify?
summary: Conformal prediction (CP) is a post-hoc calibration method that returns prediction sets with distribution-free coverage guarantees, and the size of the output set is often interpreted as a notion of uncertainty. We show that the difference in set size between full and split CP is directly connected to Bayesian posterior variance, which is the epistemic uncertainty of the model. Essentially, this difference in set size is an aggregation of two opposite effects: (1) better model accuracy and therefore smaller set size achieved by training over extra calibration points, and (2) the "formability" of the model at test point towards every possible label. The latter effect vanishes with stronger models or more calibration data (as epistemic uncertainty is known for that behavior). It turns out that the model's formability itself (without the quantization effect of prediction sets, and through estimating the posterior variance) is a useful tool to quantify the epistemic uncertainty. In our empirical evaluation it performs on par with the state of the art in many setups.
core_methodology: Conformal prediction (CP) as a post-hoc calibration method for quantifying epistemic uncertainty through prediction set size differences
data_sources: Not specified (theoretical paper)
alpha_potential: Potential use in quantifying model uncertainty for trading algorithms, particularly in dynamic decision-making where uncertainty estimation impacts position sizing or model switching
title_cn: 保形预测量化何种“形式”的不确定性？
summary_cn: 本研究通过对比完整与分割保形预测的集合大小差异，揭示了该方法量化模型认知不确定性的机制。在量化交易中可应用于：1) 动态风险评估模型 2) 算法交易中的自适应仓位管理 3) 多模型融合策略的权重分配

title: Contrastive Adversarial Training for Robust Graph Neural Networks under Label Poisoning
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are effective for modeling relational data but are vulnerable to label poisoning, where a small number of corrupted training labels can propagate errors across the graph via message passing. Despite this risk, defenses against label poisoning remain underexplored: existing methods are primarily designed for label noise and often rely on robust losses or heuristic data cleaning that fail to distinguish adversarial poisoning from naturally hard examples. In this paper, we propose CoLAT (Contrastive Label-flipping for Adversarial Training), a novel contrastive adversarial training framework tailored for robust node classification on graphs. The core of our approach is a structure-aware detection model that uses contrastive learning to identify label-structure inconsistencies. Unlike prior contrastive methods that focus on representation learning, CoLAT leverages contrastive embeddings to select high-risk nodes that guide adversarial label-flipping during training. This alternating optimization not only performs structure-aware adversarial training but also implicitly sanitizes some corrupted labels, improving robustness against diverse attacks from the literature. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that CoLAT consistently outperforms existing defenses under various poisoning intensities while scaling efficiently to large graphs.
core_methodology: Contrastive adversarial training framework for robust node classification on graphs, specifically designed to detect and mitigate label poisoning attacks in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The method leverages contrastive learning to identify label-structure inconsistencies and performs adversarial label-flipping during training.
data_sources: Benchmark datasets for node classification tasks, potentially applicable to relational financial data such as credit networks, transaction networks, or asset correlation graphs.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve the robustness of GNN-based trading models against adversarial attacks or noisy labels in financial datasets. Could enhance reliability in applications like fraud detection, credit scoring, or asset correlation modeling.
title_cn: 基于对抗性标签翻转的对比对抗训练用于鲁棒图神经网络
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新型对比对抗训练框架CoLAT，旨在提高图神经网络（GNN）在标签污染攻击下的鲁棒性。通过结合对比学习和对抗训练，该方法有效识别并修复标签-结构不一致问题，可提升金融领域关系型数据模型（如信用网络分析、资产关联建模）的可靠性。

title: A Statistical Viewpoint on Adam, Shampoo and Muon
summary: We provide new statistical insights into designing stochastic optimization methods. By modeling the gradient via a normal distribution, we argue that the stochastic gradient should be whitened using its covariance. We give an online method for estimating the mean and variance of the gradients based on regularized likelihood or, equivalently, through a maximum a posteriori estimate. We then show how to use structured approximations to the covariance within this same framework, which includes diagonal and Kronecker-factored approximations. The diagonal approximation results in a method that is very closely related to Adam and performs as well in practice. The Kronecker approximation results in the new MN method, which is a variant of Shampoo and KL-Shampoo. We also recover Muon by applying this same statistical framework to the gradient direction rather than the full gradient. By combining this with a whitening step, we arrive at MN-Muon, a novel preconditioned version of Muon. Our experiments on GPT-2-type models at Chinchilla scale indicate that MND, the diagonal implementation of MN, outperforms both the Distributed Shampoo and the KL-Shampoo implementations in terms of stability, final validation loss and time taken. MND-Muon, the diagonal implementation of MN-Muon, improves on Muon in 21 of 24 paired GPT-small runs and achieves a lower best validation loss on GPT-medium, where it remains stable over the six tested learning rates. However, we found that NorMuon was comparable to MND-Muon and achieved a slightly lower validation loss on GPT-medium and at GPT-small batch 512 on FineWeb.
core_methodology: The paper presents a statistical approach to stochastic optimization by modeling gradients with normal distributions and whitening them using covariance. It introduces methods like MN and MN-Muon, which are variants and improvements over existing optimization techniques like Adam and Shampoo.
data_sources: The paper experiments on GPT-2-type models, which are not directly related to financial data, but the methodology could be adapted for financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The optimization techniques could potentially enhance the training of machine learning models in quantitative finance, leading to better predictive models for trading strategies. However, direct application to financial data is not demonstrated.
title_cn: 关于Adam、Shampoo和Muon的统计观点
summary_cn: 本文从统计角度设计随机优化方法，通过正态分布建模梯度并利用协方差进行白化处理，提出了改进的优化算法MN和MN-Muon。虽然实验基于GPT-2模型，但其方法可应用于金融数据的机器学习模型优化，提升交易策略的预测性能。

title: FHKAN: Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Learning
summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) replace fixed scalar weights by learnable univariate maps, yet most spectral KANs still rely on Chebyshev polynomials that live on a bounded interval and therefore require a saturating squashing of the pre-activation. We introduce the Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (FHKAN), a neural architecture that equips KANs with an adaptive, trainable fractional-order generalized Hermite basis. With a nonnegative shape parameter, the underlying generalized Hermite functions are orthonormal on the entire real line and uniformly bounded under a Gaussian envelope, so they act directly on unbounded pre-activations without any saturating map. We derive closed-form derivatives of the generalized, fractional, and scaled basis away from the origin and determine its order of differentiability at the origin, where the fractional power map creates a singular point. On synthetic regression, FHKAN attains the lowest test error at every network depth among nine fixed activations and the spline-based KAN. On image classification, image denoising, and sentiment analysis, the best-performing fractional Hermite block yields the highest accuracy or reconstruction quality. On physics-informed problems, FHKAN reaches mean absolute errors of order 10^-6 to 10^-5 on the Lane-Emden equation, residuals of order 10^-4 on the Burgers equation, and absolute errors below 10^-4 on a fractional delay differential equation.
core_methodology: FHKAN uses a neural architecture with adaptive fractional-order generalized Hermite basis functions, which are orthonormal on the entire real line and uniformly bounded under a Gaussian envelope, to handle unbounded pre-activations without squashing. It was tested on synthetic regression, image classification, denoising, sentiment analysis, and physics-informed problems.
data_sources: Potentially applicable to any quantitative trading data that requires robust function approximation, such as financial time series, order book data, and sentiment analysis.
alpha_potential: The adaptive nature of the Hermite basis could enable better modeling of financial time series with fat tails and non-linear relationships, particularly in high-frequency trading and volatility prediction.
title_cn: FHKAN：基于分阶赫米特-科尔莫戈罗夫-阿诺德网络的数据驱动和物理信息学习
summary_cn: FHKAN是一种新型神经网络架构，通过引入可训练的分阶赫米特基函数，直接在无界预激活上操作，无需限幅。该方法在金融时间序列建模中具有潜力，特别是高频交易和波动率预测，能够更好地捕捉非线性关系和厚尾特性。

title: Mining the Self-Rewriting System: A Vision for Data Mining on AI-Native Infrastructure
summary: Classical data mining treats data as generated outside the learner. Emerging AI-native infrastructure invalidates this assumption: as agents observe system state, act, update retrieval stores and models, and promote new artifacts into the serving path, their own decisions reshape the future logs, traces, corpora, and evaluation records used for later training and release. We call this new research object a self-rewriting system and the resulting system-induced distribution shift endogenous drift. Our central, falsifiable claim is that cross-surface causes are not identifiable in general from marginal per-surface monitoring: different coupled failures can produce the same individual signals while differing in their joint behavior, requiring joint analysis for reliable attribution. This agenda comprises four foundational research problems: fusing heterogeneous drift signals into calibrated gating and attribution (C1); mining agent traces whose activity alphabet evolves (C2); maintaining knowledge fabrics through online reindexing, faithfulness, and compression decisions (C3); and safely promoting concurrent learning streams through one shared evaluation gate (C4). These remain fragmented across concept drift, performative prediction, process mining, streaming retrieval-augmented generation, and MLOps, without a unified data-mining agenda. We outline public benchmarks and evaluation criteria, using AI-native telecom only as a motivating exemplar with analogues in finance, software CI/CD, and clinical decision support.
core_methodology: Focuses on addressing endogenous drift in AI-native systems through joint analysis of heterogeneous drift signals, evolving activity alphabets, knowledge fabric maintenance, and concurrent learning stream promotion
data_sources: System logs, traces, corpora, and evaluation records from AI-native infrastructure (potentially applicable to financial data streams)
alpha_potential: Potential to detect and correct for self-referential data drift in AI-driven trading systems, improving model robustness in dynamic markets
title_cn: 自重写系统的挖掘：AI原生基础设施上数据挖掘的愿景
summary_cn: 该论文研究AI原生系统中的数据偏移问题（内生性漂移），提出了跨信号联合分析方法。对量化交易的价值在于改善AI交易系统在自我影响数据环境中的鲁棒性，可能提升策略在动态市场中的持续有效性。

title: CVaR-RMD: CVaR Selection Pressure for Robust Metaheuristic Discovery
summary: Large language models have recently been used to discover heuristics through iterative program search, offering a promising approach to automated algorithm design. However, candidates selected by average performance may degrade across instance families, random seeds, and problem scales because mean-based objectives can obscure rare but severe failures. We propose CVaR-RMD, a risk-sensitive evolutionary framework that uses an LLM to mutate executable heuristic programs and ranks candidates by empirical conditional value-at-risk over heterogeneous evaluation conditions. Across three combinatorial optimization domains, CVaR-based selection improves upper-tail performance and reduces failure rates while maintaining competitive mean performance. These gains persist on larger unseen instances and independently curated within-domain benchmarks
core_methodology: The paper proposes CVaR-RMD, a risk-sensitive evolutionary framework that uses an LLM to mutate executable heuristic programs and ranks candidates by empirical conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) over heterogeneous evaluation conditions.
